or even departure to a foreign land. He who climbs alone upon a tree that bears milk or fruit [shall suffer likewise].
Remaining there, one should awaken; for such a person, success is ordained.
He who ascends a palace, a bull, a boat, a couch, an elephant,
or a mountain at the end of a dream, for him success is ordained.
Alternatively, falling from any one of these is a sign of death.
For there may indeed be loss of wealth, mental anguish, or even imprisonment.
If one sees a seat, a bed, a house, a garment,
or likewise a cloak, blazing in a dream, his success is ordained.
[Furthermore,] those that are well-worn, broken, or both flaming and extinguished— *9th line*— [if seen in a dream, success is ordained].
The seer is not established in a dream, nor are the hands and the fruits of action.
If one sees in a dream a garment with a hole, a deceptive cloak, or likewise one's own upper garment, or [a garment] smelling of the cardinal directions, one does not succeed. However,
very beautiful garments that are flawless and new—
If one conquers by means of knowledge in a dream, its accomplishment is ordained for him.
One shall obtain white ointment, garlands, parasols, seats, and banners;
conchs, lotuses, [and other auspicious signs].
White substances, milk, curd, ghee, fresh meat, and fruits—these are likewise obtained.
But for him who eats at the end of the dream, success is ordained.
Having seen oneself traveling through the sky in a dream, or likewise having sexual intercourse with a forbidden woman,
or even seeing one's own excrement, one shall attain spiritual perfection (*siddhi*).
Whether one recites mantras, performs fire-oblations, weeps, or even dies [in such a dream], [the same result follows].
Whether one kills or performs a sacrifice, one shall attain accomplishment even in a dream.
He who drinks a garland of flowers, honeyed wine, or the ocean of milk at the end of a dream,
for him success is ordained.
He who sees in a dream while lying down the destruction of his cattle, horses, or land, or weapons, ornaments, and elephants, finds no success.
Furthermore, by obtaining these, one shall attain desired objects;
provided that one does not look at them for one's own husband until the sun has risen.
He who climbs upon a withered tree, or one that is variegated, or even one covered in thorns at the end of his dream, for him no success is found.
If a man enters the fire at the end of his sleep,
or even if he suffers a loss of memory, no accomplishment is attained by him.

He who sees ashes, charcoal, bones, hair, soot, or a black serpent at the end of his sleep is ordained to attain success. He who, having eaten vegetables, oil, or black fruit, sleeps at night [sees these things].
And he attains neither success, nor happiness, nor prosperity.
He who, at the end of a dream, mounts a bear, a camel, a man, a donkey, a mule, or a wolf, finds no success. Furthermore,
[dreams of] anointing with oil, marriage, obtaining a son, or setting out on a journey [are likewise inauspicious].
Having seen singing, laughter, and dancing in a dream, one does not attain success.
One who perceives oneself as excessively corpulent, seized by impurity, afflicted by disease, poorly clad,
and [unfortunate] due to a bad dream, succeeds [in the practice]. Or [one sees] a mendicant,
or one born of the lowest caste, or one afflicted by disease, or one dressed in red garments.
Furthermore, having seen oneself as insane or facing destruction in a dream, one does not attain success.
If, in a dream, one is deficient in a limb, afflicted by a disorder, or covered in impurities;
or if one remains naked in that [dream], for such a person no success is found.
O you whose nature is the head, where are you going? For in non-existence, nothing is desired.
When spoken thus, it is not established whether [the object] exists in a human dream or as a direct perception.
Likewise, if in a dream one voids urine or feces, or [sees] gold or silver, or the row of teeth falls out, he too does not attain success.
If one sees these things as inverted or as mere names while lying in a dream, for him no success is found.
Just as a Vaiśya maiden, a queen, or a Brahmin woman who is well-disposed,
so too for a king, a Brahmin, or even an ascetic, success is ordained.

Having seen in a dream a king endowed with virtuous conduct, a Brahmin who has mastered the Vedas, or a woman possessed of auspicious marks, one’s success is assured. A woman wearing white garments, adorned with white garlands and unguents, [is likewise a sign of success].
For whomsoever one performs this rite at the end of a dream, for that person prosperity shall be manifest in every direction.
If one seizes a woman wearing black garments, adorned with black garlands and unguents,
at the end of a dream, no success whatsoever shall be found for that person.
A woman wearing red garments, adorned with red garlands and unguents—
Likewise, he who is seized in a dream does not succeed either.

One who is seen in a dream wearing rags, covered in filth, afflicted by disease, or having a deformed face—whosoever is thus encountered in a dream does not attain success. Thus have the dreams been described by me; now the procedure for them, O Six-faced One, shall be told.
They speak of the future exactly as it is, O Yuktakarṇa.
Upon seeing an auspicious or inauspicious dream at the end of the night, one should perform a thousand [recitations];
in the middle of the night, half of that; and at the beginning, one hundred, in other cases as well.
Even for one whose nature is Śiva, if a bad dream occurs, he should perform the rite with double the [usual] materials. "One whose nature is Śiva" means the Guru.
[This refers to] the student's entrance and so forth.

Having performed the satiation (*tarpaṇa*) and illumination (*dīpana*) of the mantras as before, having offered the internal oblation (*antarbali*), and having worshipped Śiva and requested permission for the disciple’s entry,

he should place the Hand of Śiva (*śivahasta*) upon his own head, adorn himself with the turban (*uṣṇīṣa*) and other ornaments, contemplate "I am Śiva," and having gone outside, [he should address] the disciple.

Having caused [the disciple] to enter according to the rules, seated him near the fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*), and worshipped him, one should meditate as before for the purpose of joining the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*). Having performed the *saṃpāta-homa* upon the head of the disciple and offered a hundred oblations with the root mantra, one should give the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
Then, having raised the disciple and offered three oblations into the fire with the root mantra, one should perform worship toward the jar (*kumbha*), the mandala, and the Guru.

Having had [the cord] prepared, he should bring the *pāśasūtra* located near Ghaṭeśvara to the disciple; having consecrated the cord with sprinkling (*saṃprokṣya*), worshipped and offered libations (*santarpya*) to Śiva in the fire as before, tied it to the disciple’s crest-lock (*śikhā*), honored the disciple, and projected the channels (*nāḍī*) and other elements onto the cord, [he should cast it] into the fire.

Having offered oblations for the sake of satisfaction (*tṛptyarthaṃ*) to ensure the presence [of the deity], one should contemplate the entire path (*samastādhvan*) as residing within the body of the thread. Then,

for the sake of unifying all the paths that have been deposited in the self, the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), the mandala, and so forth, one should offer one hundred and eight oblations with the root mantra and present the final full oblation (*pūrṇā*).

(The purification of the nivṛtti-kalā): Following that, having placed [the mantra] "Hāṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), and having worshipped it, one should satisfy it with [the mantra] ending in svāhā.
One should perform the visualization and so forth in the sequence beginning with *nivṛtti*. It is as follows: *Hāṃ Hlāṃ*.

Salutation to the one who is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurity (*mala*), karma (*karman*), *māyā*, and the *māyeya* assistants; to the one whose form is feminine and whose form is the principle;
salutation to the bond of the *kalā* of *nivṛtti*—thus [one should recite] in its own place.
One should contemplate the womb containing the association of the fourteen kinds of beings, beginning with the immobile and ending with Brahmā. The creation of beings consists of eight variations;
the divine and animal births are fivefold, and human birth is [the remaining one].
And the elemental creation is, in brief, of one kind. Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ!

To the one who possesses the principles, the worlds, the phonemes, the words, the mantras, impurity, karma, māyā, and that which is born of māyā as his attendants; to the one whose form is the principle of the female;
to the noose of the kalā of Nivṛtti—huṃ phaṭ! (3rd line)

Having performed the striking and piercing in its own place, one should enter with this mantra ending in *namaḥ*: *hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ*, [obeisance] to the principle (*tattva*), the world (*bhuvana*), the phoneme (*varṇa*), the word (*pada*), and the mantra; to the impurity of action (*malakarma*); to Māyā and her attendants (*māyeyasaciva*); to that which has the form of a woman (*strīrūpa*) as the form of the principle;
and to the noose of the *nivṛtti-kalā*.

Having performed the separation with "huṃ phaṭ," one should draw in the noose using the *pūraka* breath and the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* with this mantra ending in *svāhā*: *hauṃ hlāṃ hāṃ hauṃ*, [to] the one whose ministers are the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurities (*mala*), actions (*karman*), time (*yāma*), illusion (*māyā*), and the principle of ego (*ahaṃkāra*).
To the one whose form is the reality of the female principle, to the bond of the *nivṛtti-kalā*, *haḥ huṃ phaṭ*— with this, by means of the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breathing technique],
having grasped the bond of the *nivṛtti-kalā* below the knees with *hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ*,

[one offers it] to the one whose form is the reality of the female principle, who possesses the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and the assistants of *māyā*.

"Salutation to Nivṛttikalāpāśa. Having thus joined [the deity] with the Cetakodbhava-mudrā in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), having worshipped him, and having offered the arghya with that mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should invoke his presence and offer five oblations (*āhuti*). Thereafter, having invoked Brahmā into the pit with "Hāṃ, salutation to Brahmā," having worshipped him, and having offered five oblations with that mantra ending in *svāhā*—

"O Brahman, under your authority in this matter, I shall undergo initiation for the sake of liberation; you must remain favorable [to me] so that I may inform the Lord of the ritual. Then, having dismissed Brahmā, [he recites]: *hāṃ hlāṃ hauṃ hāṃ* to the one who possesses the principles (*tattva*), the worlds (*bhuvana*), the armor (*varma*), the stages (*pada*), the mantras, impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and the assistants of *māyā*.

Having placed Vāgīśvarī— she who is the pervasive Mistress of Speech, for the sake of the noose of the power of cessation (*nivṛttikalā*), and who is menstruating and clad in red garments— within the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), and having worshipped her, one should satisfy her with that [mantra] ending in *svāhā*,
display the *yonimudrā*, and [recite]: *hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ*.

Having installed and worshipped Vāgīśvara— the agitator of his own source, who possesses ten arms and five faces, and who is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and the products of *māyā* (*māyeya*), as well as the pervasive bonds of the *nivṛtti*-kalā— by reciting "Salutation to Vāgīśvara," and having gratified him with that [mantra] ending in *svāhā*.
Having visualized Vāgīśvarī as the one who simultaneously gives birth to many births from various wombs, and having visualized the union of the two,
[one should recite] "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ | Astrāya Huṃ Phaṭ," and with the Nārāca-mudrā, [one should strike] the animal-consciousness residing in the Nivṛtti-kalā with a flower.

Having struck [it] with "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ Astrāya Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā," and having offered five oblations with "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ Astrāya Huṃ Phaṭ," [one should contemplate] the consciousness of the bound soul (*paśu*) situated in *nivṛtti*.

Having performed five oblations with that [mantra] ending in *svāhā* after piercing [the site], one should deposit and worship [the deity] in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with: *haṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ namaḥ*, *hāṃ vāmāyai namaḥ*.
Then, having offered five oblations with *huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ hāṃ vāmāyai svāhā*, one offers to Vāmā with *hāṃ namaḥ*.

Having gone out with the *recaka* [breath] while reciting *hāṃ haṃ huṃ phaṭ hiṃ jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ*, one should place [the mantra] in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), worship it, and offer five oblations (*pañcāhutīḥ*) with *hāṃ huṃ hūṃ hīṃ jyeṣṭhāyai svāhā*. Then, having separated the consciousness of the bound soul (*paśu*) residing in the thread from Jyeṣṭhā, one should recite *hāṃ hūṃ namaḥ*.

Having placed [the syllable] "HŪṂ RAUDRYAI NAMAḤ" in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and worshipped it with "HĀṂ HŪṂ NAMAḤ," and having offered five oblations with "HĀṂ RAUDRYAI SVĀHĀ," one should extract the self—
which consists of the eightfold city (puryaṣṭaka)— by means of Raudrī, lead it to the dvādaśānta, and [utter] "HŪṂ HĀṂ HAṂ."
"I grasp the consciousness of the animal. Having grasped the consciousness with "Haḥ Huṃ Phaṭ," having taken it up with the *puraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breath],

having established it within one's own self, and having led it to one's own *dvādaśānta*, one should then take it from there and visualize it resting in the *kuṇḍa*, supported by the *vāma* and other winds.
Hāṃ haṃ hāṃ! O Ātman,
being joined for the sake of the impregnation (*garbhādhāna*) into the wombs of all the worlds within the realm of *nivṛtti-kalā* according to your own karma—
thus [you enter] into Bhuvana-vāgīśvarī, who possesses the form of manifold wombs and is simultaneously divided by the distinctions of many wombs.
Having joined [the syllables] for the sake of accomplishing the manifestation of the form according to the karma—namely, *hāṃ haṃ ātmane namaḥ*—one should worship in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having offered libations with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should perform five or five oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*) during the libation. Then, for the sake of union, having offered five oblations with the root mantra, [one offers] *hāṃ* for the sake of the simultaneous union of this soul (*aṇu*).

One should pray, "Let it be performed. Then, having reflected upon the birth of the sacrificial animal from its various origins, one offers five oblations with the *hṛdaya-mantra* ending in *svāhā*, while visualizing: "I effect the birth of the animal simultaneously from all its origins," and offers five oblations with the *śiras-mantra* ending in *svāhā*.

Having reflected, "I shall establish the animal's entitlement to experience [the fruits of its actions] everywhere simultaneously," one should offer five oblations with the *śikhā* mantra ending in *svāhā*.
Then, from the beginningless cycle of transmigration of the animal until this very day, regarding the actions that have arisen, those karmas already experienced—

Having abandoned [the previous rites], one should contemplate, "I shall accomplish enjoyment in accordance with all remaining karmas, which abide in the world of *nivṛtti-kalā*," and offer five oblations (*pañcāhuti*) with the armor-mantra (*kavaca*) ending in *svāhā*. In this interval, among the forty sacraments (*saṃskāra*) beginning with *garbhādhāna* and ending with *anteṣṭi*, [one performs] the sixteen intermediate sacraments suitable for Śaiva yoga.
Since the consecration of renunciation (*saṃnyāsa-saṃskāra*) occurs subsequent to the initiation into *nirvāṇa*, and since the funeral rite (*antyeṣṭi*) occurs immediately after the fall of the body,
[one should perform] the remaining consecrations for the specific initiations pertaining to each respective stage of life (*āśrama*), distinct from those two.

One should perform [the rites] as previously stated. For one who is renouncing [the world], one should perform [them] up to the final saṃskāra of the forest-dweller (vānaprastha). Which are those? They are:

conception (garbhādhāna), the rite for a male child (puṃsavana), the parting of the hair (sīmantonnayana), birth-rites (jātakarman), naming (nāmakaraṇa), the first outing (niṣkramaṇa), the first feeding of solid food (annaprāśana), the tonsure (caula), and initiation (upanayana).

The sixteen sacraments (*saṃskāras*) consist of: [the birth rites], the naming, the first feeding, the tonsure, the sacred thread ceremony (*upanayana*), the observances (*vratas*), the gift of a cow (*godāna*), the return home (*samāvartana*), marriage, the stage of the forest-dweller (*vānaprastha*), renunciation (*sannyāsa*), and the funeral rite (*antyeṣṭi*).
This has been stated in the *Acintyaviśvasādākhya*: [Text from the Acintyaviśvasādākhya]
And at the rite of conception (*garbhādhāna*), and at the first pregnancy ceremony (*puṃsavana*),
as well as at the parting of the hair (*sīmantonnayana*), the birth-rite (*jātakarman*), the naming ceremony (*nāman*),
the rite of going out of the house (*niṣkrāmaṇa*), the first feeding of solid food (*annaprāśana*), and the tonsure ceremony (*caulakarman*).
The sacred thread is worn over the left shoulder at the time of the instruction of vows, at the ceremony of giving away a cow, and at the rite of ritual bathing.
"In marriage, in forest-dwelling, and in the state of a female ascetic at Nandikeśvara"—thus [ends] the section on the remaining [rites].
Because it pertains specifically to Brahmins, it has not been written here. Having thus performed the purificatory rites (saṃskāras) and having mentally removed their obstacles...

In the same manner, one should perform the withdrawal with three oblations. Thereafter, having contemplated dissolution (*laya*)—which consists of supreme delight in the objects of enjoyment—one should offer five oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*), saying: "O Blessed One, effect for this self a dissolution in the form of supreme delight regarding the objects of enjoyment; effect it, effect it! This is the commencement of the activity of *māyā*. For the purification of those [objects], one offers five oblations with the root mantra.
"O Blessed One, having offered [this],

one should request that the Guru perform the purification of the stream of undertakings resulting from one's own illusory activity for the sake of enjoyment; since one experiences [the results] through karma,
[the purification] is for the sake of non-rebirth, being purified by the reality of cessation."

One should perform five oblations with the *hṛdaya* mantra. For the sake of purification—namely, the removal of [the karmic residues of] caste, lifespan, experience, and impressions—one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*) and the *hṛdaya*, while reflecting: "O Blessed One, through this expiation (*niṣkṛti*), may I practice purity in all actions.
(3rd line)
Having conceived the separation of the self’s power of withdrawal from the bondage of the *puryaṣṭaka* due to the absence of the worlds—
a separation consisting of its exiting outward— one should offer five oblations with the root mantra accompanied by the *Pāśupata* mantra ending in *svāhā*,
[thereby removing] the form characterized by attachment to the objects of enjoyment.

Having contemplated the impurity (*mala*) and karma (*karman*), and for the purpose of concealing them, one should offer a hundred oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, followed by ten oblations with the *pāśupata-mantra*.

Having resolved that the separation from *māyā* has been achieved—consisting merely of the cessation of the impurities of *nivṛtti-kalā* and karma—one should again offer five oblations with the *mūla-mantra* in the same manner. Then, holding the thread with the index finger and thumb, [one should perform the rite] for the bound soul (*paśu*).

"By the movement of the cord of the noose, I shall effect the loosening of the noose. Having thus contemplated, one should offer five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*. Then, having consecrated the scissors seven times with the weapon-mantra, [reciting] *haṃ hlāṃ*...

"Hāṃ! [I bow to] that which has as its assistants the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurity (*mala*), karma, and *māyā*; which has the form of the principle of woman (*strīrūpatattva*);

[and] which severs the noose of the *kalā* of cessation (*nivṛtti*). Huṃ haḥ! For the weapon (*astra*), huṃ phaṭ!"—with this, one should cut with the scissors. Having said, "I perform the crushing of the fetter (*pāśa*) of the bound soul (*paśu*)," [one recites]: "Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ."

I crush the bonds of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impure karma (*malakarma*), *māyā*, and the products of *māyā* (*māyeya*), as well as the bond of the fetters (*kalāpāśa*) that takes the form of woman and the form of the principles. Saying "Huṃ haḥ, for the weapon, huṃ phaṭ," and having wiped away the bond with both hands, one says, "I make the bond of the bound soul (*paśu*) circular," and [recites] "Hāṃ hlāṃ..."
"Hāṃ! I make circular the principles, worlds, phonemes, words, mantras, impurity, māyā, and the assistants of māyā; the principle in the form of woman;
and the noose of the kalā of cessation—huṃ haḥ, for the weapon, huṃ phaṭ! Having thus made it circular with both hands.
Having said, "I burn [it]," and having placed the noose at the tip of the *sruva* ladle filled with clarified butter, [he recites]: *hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ*, [burning] the principles (*tattva*),

worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and its attendants (*māyeya-saciva*), as well as the principle in the form of woman (*strīrūpa-tattvarūpa*) and the cessation of rebirth (*nivṛtti*).

(………) Having offered oblations with the mantra *haṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, one should burn [the residue]. Then, to remove the noose and the hook (*pāśāṅkuśa*), one should offer five oblations with the Astra-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*. For the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should offer eight oblations with the same Astra-mantra, preceded by *svāhā* at the end. Then, having worshipped Brahmā in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the Heart-mantra, one should [proceed] with that same [mantra] ending in *svāhā*.

Having satisfied [the deities] with *hāṃ*, and having offered five oblations with the mantra: "O Brahman, O Lord of the principles (*tattva*), worlds, phonemes, words, and mantras; O you who possess impurity, karma, and *māyā*; O consort of the principles of *māyā* and its derivatives; O you whose form is the principle of the female (*strīrūpa-tattva-rūpā*); accept this [offering], *svāhā*!"—[he addresses] Brahmā, the Lord of the *nādya* and *kalā* [principles], for the sake of this bound soul (*paśu*).
Furthermore, having requested Brahmā, saying, "By the command of Śiva, you must not place any obstacle within my sphere," he should dismiss him. Then, saying,

"I shall perform the extraction of the sacrificial animal (paśu)," and having offered five oblations with the root mantra ending in *svāhā*, he should proceed by the *vāmā* [channel] and separate himself from the *jyeṣṭhā* [channel].
Having extracted the self from the *kumbha* by means of the body of primordial nature (*prakṛti*), which consists of the Rudras and other [deities],

and visualizing it as standing like the autumn moon slightly released from Rāhu, one should establish it within oneself; then, having projected the consciousness of the disciple onto the cord of the noose, [one should perform] with the root mantra for the sake of stabilizing the self.

Having offered five oblations for the nourishment of the disciple, one should sprinkle water from the *arghya* vessel—which consists of drops of nectar—upon his head with the ring finger while reciting the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. Then, having gratified Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara with ten oblations each and having dismissed them, one should offer the *pūrṇāhuti*. Thereafter: *hāṃ hlāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ*.

Having performed the conjunction of the pure and the impure by pronouncing the short and long vowels with "Nivṛtti-Pratiṣṭhā-Kalābhyāṃ Namaḥ," one should offer five oblations with the root mantra for its stabilization. [The impure] is dissolved into the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā of the pure-impure.
Having meditated [upon this], one should offer five oblations with the root mantra. Thus is the purification of the *nivṛtti-kalā*.
(The purification of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*:
Then, having contemplated the bonds (*pāśa*) of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* as before, containing the five paths (*pañcādhvan*), [one recites] *hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ*.

Salutation to the one whose nature consists of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras; who has as his assistants the *māyā* and the products of *māyā*; and who is the bond of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* in the form of the principle of woman. Thus, having observed the existence beginning from the immobile [creation] up to Viṣṇu at the end of the cycle of emanation in its own place, [one recites]: *hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ*.

Having performed the striking (*tāḍana*) upon its own locus with the mantra "haḥ huṃ phaṭ" for the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalā— which has as its assistants the principles (*tatva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and that which pertains to *māyā* (the *māyeya*), and which takes the form of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*)— and having performed the piercing (*bhedana*) with this same mantra ending in *namaḥ*, [one should enter].

(…) Having performed the specific [rite] with "HĀṂ HVĪṂ HĀṂ TATTVABHUVANAVARṆAPADAMANTRAMALAKARMAMĀYĀMĀYEYASACIVĀYA STRĪRŪPATATVARŪPĀYA PRATIṢṬHĀKALĀPĀŚĀYA HAḤ HUṂ PHAṬ," and having drawn in the *pāśa* (bond) by means of this mantra ending in *svāhā* while employing the *pūraka* (inhalation) and the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, [one recites]: HĀṂ HVĪṂ HĀṂ.
In the world of Tatva (the third line),
for the one who possesses the ministers of *mala*, *karma*, and *māyā* along with their derivatives (*māyeya*), whose form is the reality of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva-rūpa*),
and who is the noose of the *kalās* of *Pratiṣṭhā*— [I offer] *haḥ*, *huṃ*, *phaṭ* with the inhalation (*pūraka*) and withdrawal (*saṃhāriṇī*) [breath] below the navel.

Having grasped the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā* kalā, and having uttered [the mantra] beginning with *hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ* and ending with *tatvarūpāya*, saying "Salutation to the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā* kalā," one should place it in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) using the *recakodbhava* mudrā, worship it, and offer the *arghya* with this mantra ending in *svāhā*.
For the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity,

one should offer five oblations. Thereafter, having invoked Viṣṇu into the sacrificial pit with "Hāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu" and worshipped him, one should offer five oblations with that same mantra, ending with "svāhā."
"O Viṣṇu, within this domain of yours, I shall initiate you who desire liberation.
You must remain ever-attentive; thus one should inform Viṣṇu.

Having dismissed Viṣṇu with the mantra *hlāṃ hvīṃ hlāṃ hauṃ* for the sake of the presiding deity of the principles (*tattva*), the enjoyer of the principles, and the [deities] of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*) along with their attendants.

Having placed Vāgīśvarī— red-clad and in her menses— within the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the mantra "Salutation to Vāgīśvarī, who pervades the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* and the *pāśa*," and having worshipped her,
one should satisfy her with this [mantra] ending in *svāhā*, display the *yonimudrā*, and [recite]: *hāṃ hvīṃ hauṃ hāṃ*.

"Salutation to Vāgīśvara, who possesses the principles, worlds, phonemes, words, mantras, impurities, karma, Māyā, and the adjuncts of Māyā; who is the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā* kalā; who is all-pervading. Thus [one should worship] the ten-armed one. One should [worship] the five-faced Vāgīśvara, the agitator of the remainder of the two, in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*) and worship, and having gratified Vāgīśvara with this [mantra] ending in *svāhā*, one should simultaneously contemplate the progenitor of births in many wombs and contemplate the union of the two. Then, with the weapon-mantra *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, one should strike the animal-consciousness (*paśucaitanya*) residing in the *pratiṣṭhā* level with the *nārāca-mudrā* and the *puṣpa* [mantra], saying *hāṃ haṃ*.

Having offered five oblations with *hāṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, and having pierced the manifold consciousness residing in the stage of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* with *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ astrāya haṃ phaṭ*, one should again offer five oblations with *hāṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

Having placed [the mantra] "huṃ hāṃ haṃ bhāṃ huṃ namaḥ hāṃ vāmāyai namaḥ" in the center of the *kuṇḍa* and worshipped it, and having offered five oblations with "huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ vāmāyai svāhā," one should proceed with the exhalation (*recaka*) while reciting "hāṃ namaḥ" to Vāmā; then, in the *kuṇḍa*, [one should offer] "hāṃ haṃ huṃ phaṭ hīṃ jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ."

Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*) and worship, and having offered five oblations with the mantra *hāṃ haṃ huṃ phaṭ hīṃ jyeṣṭhāyai svāhā*, one should separate the consciousness of the sacrificial animal (*paśu*) from Jyeṣṭhā within the thread,
and then place [the mantras] in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with: *hāṃ huṃ namaḥ* and *hrūṃ raudryai namaḥ*.

Having offered five oblations with the mantra *hūṃ hāṃ hūṃ namaḥ hrūṃ raudryai svāhā*, one should extract the self—the embodied primordial nature (*prakṛti*) consisting of the three qualities—into the form of Raudrī; having led it to the end of the twelve (*dvādaśānta*), one should seize that consciousness with the mantra *hrūṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ paśucaitanyaṃ gṛhṇāmi haḥ huṃ phaṭ*. Thus, one seizes that consciousness.

Having taken [the essence] by means of the *pūraka* and *saṃhāriṇī* [breaths], having established it within one's own self, and having led it to one's own *dvādaśānta*, and having taken it from there—either after worshipping me in the *kuṇḍa* or having meditated upon that which is supported by it—one should say: "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ! O Self, become united with the rite of *garbhādhāna* in all wombs; Namaḥ!"

Thus, having joined [the syllables] with "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Ātmane Namaḥ" for the sake of accomplishing the arising of various forms within Bhuvanavāgīśvarī— who possesses many types of wombs and is simultaneously differentiated by the distinctions of those many wombs— and having worshipped her in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*),
one should satisfy her with oblations ending in "Svāhā" using this mantra, and then [offer] five oblations each with the root mantra.

Having performed the propitiation through presence (*sāṃnidhyatarpaṇa*) and offered five oblations with the root mantra for the sake of union, one should then pray: "Hauṃ! May the womb of this [deity] be joined simultaneously. Then, regarding the victim...

Having reflected, "I shall effect the conception [of the soul] simultaneously within various wombs corresponding to its karma, which culminates in the worlds of the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalā," and having offered five oblations with the mantra *svānta*... into his own heart, he should contemplate: "I shall bring about the birth of the bound soul (*paśu*) from all wombs at once."

Having offered five oblations with the *svāhā* at the end of the *śiras* mantra, and having reflected, "I grant the animal the authority to experience [the fruits of its actions] everywhere simultaneously," one should offer five oblations with the *svāhā* at the end of the *śikhā* mantra, [thinking], "From today onwards, for this animal, beginning from the beginningless cycle of saṃsāra..."

Having reflected, "I shall simultaneously bring about enjoyment in accordance with all remaining karma, beginning from the stage of *pratiṣṭhā* among the fully arisen karmas," one should offer five oblations with the armor-mantra (*kavaca*) ending in *svāhā*. Then, having contemplated, "I effect a dissolution (*laya*) in the form of supreme bliss within the objects of ordinary enjoyment for the bound soul (*paśu*)," one should offer five oblations with the root-mantra (*mūla*) to those [elements] whose forms are identical to primordial nature (*prakṛti*).

Having contemplated, "I perform the release of the channels for the purpose of removing the karma that initiates them," one offers five oblations with the Pāśupata-weapon mantra ending in *svāhā*, and then, for the purification of the principles (*tattva*), offers five oblations with the Heart mantra ending in *svāhā*.

Since there is an absence of the world-enjoyment (*bhuvana-bhoga*) of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* within the self, one should offer a hundred oblations with the *śiras* mantra ending in *svāhā* for the sake of purifying the *pratiṣṭhā*. Having visualized the self as having emerged from its original state—like the moon released from Rāhu—one should think: "I am performing the removal of the obscuration of impurity (*mala-tirodhāna*) by means of a characteristic distinct from that of the bound soul (*paśu*)."

Having reflected thus, one should offer five oblations with the root mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, grasping the cord of the bonds (*pāśasūtra*) with the index finger and the thumb, and visualizing, "I effect the separation of the bound soul (*paśu*) by moving the cord of the bonds," one should offer five oblations with the weapon mantra (*astra-mantra*) ending in *huṃ phaṭ*. Thereafter, having consecrated the knife seven times with the weapon mantra, [one recites] *hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ*.

Saying, "I am severing the bonds of the bound soul," one should cut the bond of the bound soul with the scissors while reciting: "huṃ haḥ | astrāya huṃ phaṭ," [severing] that which consists of the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), mantras, impurity (mala), karma, māyā, and the products of māyā (māyeya), as well as the form of woman and the form of the principle, and the noose of the kalās of the level of establishment (pratiṣṭhā).

Hāṃ Hiṃ Hāṃ! I crush the bonds of the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalā, which consist of the letters, words, and mantras of the principles (*tattva*) such as the worlds (*bhuvana*), along with their assistants—*mala*, *karman*, *māyā*, and *māyeya*—and which take the form of the principle of woman; Haṃ Haḥ! To the weapon, Huṃ Phaṭ! [Thus, one should recite while striking] with both hands.

Having wiped the noose of the bound soul (*paśu*) and said, "I make the noose of the bound soul circular," [one should perform the rite] with the *haṃ haḥ astrāya* mantra. (On the right side: *hāṃ* ...

"I make circular the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*, which consists of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, the assistants of *māyā*, and the principle in the form of woman.
*Haṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*—[thus with the knife].

Having formed a circle with the two syllables *huṃ* and *phaṭ*, and having said, "I burn the bond (*pāśa*) of the bound soul (*paśu*"), one places the bond at the tip of the *sruva* ladle filled with clarified butter, [reciting] *hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ* [and the principles of] the elements (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), karma, and *māyā* and its derivatives (*māyeya*).

Having offered oblations with the mantra "I burn the living one, whose form is the reality of the female principle, and who is bound by the fetters of the kalās of installation: *huṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*," one should then burn [the effigy]. Thereafter, to eliminate the sprout of the fetters, one should offer five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *phaṭ*, and for the sake of atonement, one should offer eight oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *svāhā*.

Then, having worshipped Viṣṇu in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) with the Heart-mantra ending in *svāhā*, and having gratified him with that same mantra, one offers five oblations with the following: "Hāṃ! O Viṣṇu, accept the essence (*rasa*)—which is the minister of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurity (*mala*), karma (*karman*), *māyā*, and that which is born of *māyā* (*māyeya*), and which takes the form of the principle of woman (*strīrūpa-tattva-rūpa*)—O Śukī, svāhā! Having thus offered the five oblations.

"O Viṣṇu, as this victim goes to the imperishable state with his bonds burnt away, you must perform the binding [of the remaining fetters] by your own authority, according to the command of Śiva. Having thus petitioned Viṣṇu, one should dismiss him. Then, saying "I shall effect the liberation of the victim," one should [offer oblation] with the root mantra ending in *svāhā*.

Having offered five oblations with the *Vāmā* [mantra] and the *Rocaka*, having gone to the *Jyeṣṭhā* [channel] and separated the self from *prakṛti*, having extracted the self from the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) by means of the *Raudrī* [mantra] which releases the bonds of the *kalās* and so forth, and having established it within oneself, one should project the consciousness of the disciple onto the *pāśasūtra*. Then, for the sake of stabilizing the self, one should offer five oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*).
For the nourishment of the disciple as well, one should offer the *arghya* water—which consists of drops of nectar—upon his head with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* using the ring finger.
Having gratified Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara with ten oblations, and having dismissed them with the *hṛdaya* mantra, one should offer the *pūrṇāhuti*.
Thereafter, [one should recite]: *hāṃ hvīṃ hrūṃ hāṃ pratiṣṭhā-vidyā-kalā-pāśebhyo namaḥ*.

Having performed the conjunction (*sandhāna*) of the pure and impure [elements] by means of short and long utterances, one should offer five oblations (*pañcāhuti*) for the sake of stabilizing each respective [element]. Thus ends the purification of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*.
The Purification of the Vidyā and Kalā Levels.

Thereafter, having contemplated the noose of the *vidyā-kalā* as before, containing within it the five paths (*pañcādhvan*), [one should offer salutation] with: "Hāṃ Hrūṃ Hāṃ! Salutation to the noose of the *vidyā-kalā*, which has as its attendants the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, karma, *māyā*, and that which is born of *māyā* (*māyeya*), and which takes the form of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*). [This is done] in its own place.
Having observed the womb within the womb, beginning with the immobile [elements] and ending with Rudra-garbha, one should [recite] "HĀṂ HRŪṂ HĀṂ" for the principles (tattva),

worlds (bhuvana), phonemes (varṇa), words (pada), mantras, impure karma (mala-karma), Māyā, and that which arises from Māyā (māyeya), as well as for the minister (saciva), the female form (strī-rūpa), the principle of form (tatva-rūpa), and the noose of the Vidya-kalā; then, at its own place, [one recites] "HAḤ HUṂ PHAṬ."

Having performed striking and piercing, and having entered with this mantra ending in *namaḥ*, one should effect a separation [of the bonds] with the mantra: *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*—to the one who possesses the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impure karma (*malakarma*), and *māyā* along with its attendants; to the one whose form is the principle of womanhood (*strīrūpa-tattva-rūpa*);
to the noose of the *vidyā-kalā*—with *haḥ huṃ phaṭ*. Then, one should perform inhalation (*pūraka*) with this mantra ending in *svāhā*.

Having performed the drawing-in of the noose with the *kuśa* mudrā, [one recites]: *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, to the one who possesses the principles (*tattva*), the worlds (*bhuvana*), the phonemes (*varṇa*), the words (*pada*), the mantras (*mantra*), impure karma (*malakarma*), and the illusion (*māyā*) along with its attendants (*māyeyasaciva*), to the one whose form is the principle of the female form (*strīrūpatatvarūpa*).
Having grasped the noose of the *vidyā-kalā* with the heart-mantra "haḥ huṃ phaṭ" through the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breathing technique], [one recites] "hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ."

"Salutation to the one who possesses the principles, worlds, phonemes, words, mantras, impurities, karma, *māyā*, and the *māyeya* assistants; salutation to the one whose form is the principle of womanhood and who is the noose of *vidyā* and *kalā*.

Having thus offered this mantra, ending with "svāhā," into the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) by means of the *recakodbhava-mudrā* after having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) and worship, [one should proceed].

One should offer five oblations for the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity. Having invoked Rudra into the sacrificial pit with "Hāṃ, obeisance to Rudra" and having worshipped him, one should offer five oblations with that same mantra ending in "svāhā," [reciting]:
"O Rudra, in this office of yours, I initiate this seeker of liberation."
"You should act favorably; thus you should inform Rudra.

Having dismissed Rudra with "hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ," [one should worship] with: "Obeisance to Vāgīśvarī, the pervasive one, who is the minister of the principles, worlds, phonemes, words, mantras, impurity, karma, māyā, and what is born of māyā, and who is the noose of the kalās of vidyā. [One should then visualize] Vāgīśvarī, clad in red garments and in her menses.

Having placed [the offering] in the *kuṇḍa* and having gratified it with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should display the *yonimudrā* and [recite]: *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ tatvabhuvanavarṇapadamantramalakarmamāyāmāyeyasacivāya vidyākalāpāśāya*.
"Salutation to the pervasive Lord of Speech.

Having placed the ten-armed, five-faced Lord of Speech—who agitates all wombs—within the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), and having worshipped him, one should satisfy him with this mantra ending in *svāhā*. (10th)

While contemplating Vāgīśvarī, who simultaneously gives birth to many births from various wombs, and having meditated upon their union, one should [liberate] the animal-consciousness situated within the *vidyā-kalā* with the mantra "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ Astrāya Huṃ Phaṭ" using the *nārāca-mudrā*.

Having struck with a flower while reciting "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ Astrāya Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā," and having offered five oblations with "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ Astrāya Huṃ Phaṭ," [one should contemplate] the animal-consciousness (*paśu-caitanya*) residing within the *vidyā-kalā*.

Having offered five oblations with "vibhidya hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā," and having deposited [the mantra] in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worshipped it with "huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ namaḥ" and "oṃ hāṃ vāmāyai namaḥ," one should offer five oblations with "hrūṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ hāṃ vāmāyai svāhā. Then, saying "huṃ namaḥ," one should proceed through the *vāmā* [channel] by means of exhalation (*recaka*), [ending with] "hāṃ."
Having placed [the mantra] "haṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā hīṃ jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ" in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and worshipped it,

and having offered five oblations with "hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ hiṃ jyeṣṭhāyai svāhā," one should separate the consciousness of the bound soul (paśu) residing in the thread from Jyeṣṭhā, [reciting] "hāṃ hrūṃ namaḥ; hrūṃ raudryai namaḥ."

Having placed [the deity] in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and worshipped him with "Hāṃ Hrūṃ Namaḥ," and having offered five oblations with "Hrūṃ Raudryai Svāhā," one should draw forth from the pit the Pralayākala-creature (paśu), together with the digits (kalās) and other [principles], who resembles a shimmering star; then, having drawn that soul up to the limit of the twelve (dvādaśānta)— [The remainder of the passage continues: ...one should contemplate it as being within the sphere of the heart-lotus, and then, having drawn it upward again to the limit of the twelve, one should place it within the supreme abode (dhāman). Then, having offered the oblation for the purification of the path (adhva-śuddhi-homa), one should perform the ritual of the fire-purification (agnisaṃskāra). Having led [the consciousness] with "HŪṂ HĀṂ HŪṂ PAŚUCAITANYAṂ GṚHṆĀMI HAḤ HŪṂ PHAṬ," one should seize that consciousness;
then, by means of the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breath], having established it within one's own self and led it to one's own *dvādaśānta*, one should take it from there into the *kuṇḍa*.

Having visualized the left [side] as the desired object and that which depends upon it, with the mantra "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ, O Ātman, be united for the purpose of the final consummation and the impregnation of the womb" (*namaḥ*), [one should worship] Bhuvanavāgīśvarī, who possesses many forms of wombs and is simultaneously differentiated by the distinctions of many wombs.

For the sake of accomplishing the arising of various forms, having joined [the syllables] with "hāṃ haṃ hā ātmane namaḥ," one should worship in the *kuṇḍa* and satisfy them with this mantra ending in "svāhā"; then, having performed the propitiation for the presence (*sānnidhya*) with five offerings each using the root mantra,
[one worships] those two.

Having offered five oblations with the root-mantra of conjunction (*saṃyoga*), one should pray: "Hauṃ! Let the simultaneous union of this [soul] with the subtle body (*manas*) be performed. Then, having reflected, "At one and the same time, I perform the impregnation (*garbhādhāna*) into various wombs according to the karma residing in the worlds of the *vidyā-kalā* of the bound soul (*paśu*)," one offers five oblations with the Heart-mantra ending in *svāhā*, all at once.

Having visualized, "I bring about the birth of the animal from all wombs," one should offer five oblations with the *śiras* mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, having contemplated, "I establish the animal's entitlement to enjoyments simultaneously everywhere," one should offer five oblations with the *śikhā* mantra ending in *svāhā*, [concerning] the karma accumulated by the animal throughout beginningless saṃsāra.

Having contemplated, "I shall bring about simultaneous enjoyment," and having offered five oblations with the armor-mantra (*kavaca*) ending in *svāhā*, and having reflected, "I cause the dissolution of the victim into Māyā," one offers five oblations with the root-mantra (*mūla*) ending in *svāhā*. Then, for the sake of removing the karma that initiates those streams which possess a form identical to Māyā, [one addresses] the stream of the victim...
Having contemplated, "I am practicing purification," one should offer five oblations each with the *astra-mantra* ending in *svāhā*.

Then, for the purification of the principles (*tattva-śuddhi*), one should offer five oblations with the *hṛdaya-mantra* ending in *svāhā*, [becoming] like a cloud from which the water and autumn have departed.

Having offered one hundred oblations with the *śikhā* mantra ending in *svāhā* for the sake of purifying the *vidyā-kalā*, and having reflected, "I shall perform the removal of the obscuration of impurity (*mala*) by means of the inspection (*vīkṣaṇa*) of the sacrificial animal (*paśu*)," he should offer five oblations with the root mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, taking the thread with his index finger and thumb, [he should apply it] to the sacrificial animal.
Contemplating, "By the movement of the noose-thread, I shall effect the separation from the bound soul (*paśu*)," one should offer five oblations with the Weapon mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*.
Then, having consecrated the scissors seven times with the Weapon mantra, [one recites] *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*.

Having realized that the minister in the form of the *tattva* of the female form cuts the bond (*pāśa*) consisting of the *vidyā-kalā*, one should cut the bond by performing [the rite] with "Haṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ. Having said, "I am effecting the destruction of the bonds of the bound soul (*paśu*)," one [cuts the bond] with "Hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ"—
[the minister] in the form of the *tattva* of the female form, who is the companion of *tattva*, *bhuvana*, *varṇa*, *pada*, *mantra*, *mala*, *karma*, *māyā*, and *māyeya*.
"I crush the noose of ignorance and artifice. With the mantra *hrūṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, having wiped away the noose with both hands,
[one removes] the noose of the bound soul (*paśu*).

Having said, "I am making it circular," [one recites]: *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, "I am making circular the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and its attendants (*saciva*), as well as the principle in the form of woman (*strīrūpa-tattvarūpa*) and the noose of knowledge and limited agency (*vidyā-kalā-pāśa*); *hrūṃ haḥ*. (10th line)

Having formed a circle with both hands while reciting *astrāya hūṃ phaṭ*, and saying "I burn the bond of the bound soul" (*paśoḥ pāśaṃ dahāmi*), one places the bond upon the tip of the *sruva* ladle filled with clarified butter,

[reciting]: *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, [the bond] which consists of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras, along with impurity (*mala*), karma, *māyā*, and its attendant (*māyeya-saciva*).

Having offered oblations with the mantra "I burn the bond of the kalās of the Vidyā, which has the form of the reality of the female form; Huṃ Haḥ! To the Weapon, Huṃ Phaṭ!", one should burn it. Then, for the sake of removing the bonds and the goad, one should offer five oblations with the Astra-mantra ending in "Huṃ Phaṭ".

For the purpose of expiation, one should offer eight oblations with the Astra-mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, having invoked Rudra into the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worshipped him with the Hṛdaya-mantra, one should satisfy him with that same mantra ending in *svāhā*. Having offered five oblations with "I [offer] to Rudra-tattva, Bhuvana, Varṇa, Pada, Mantra-mala, Karma, Māyā, Māyeya-saciva, Strīrūpa-tattva-rūpa, Gandha, Śukra, and Grahaṇā, svāhā," [the rite is completed].

"O Rudra, you must not again obstruct this [victim], who is bound by eight bonds and desires auspiciousness, by the command of Śaṅkara. Having thus informed Rudra, one should release him. Then, saying "I perform the liberation of the victim," one should [recite] the root mantra ending in *svāhā*.

Having offered five oblations, through the burning away of all karmas of the self, and because of the absence of illusory enjoyments, when one is liberated from Rāhu, one is like the moon emerging from autumn clouds after being obscured by them; [one emerges] from Māyā, from the lower portion of Pure Knowledge (śuddhavidyā), reaching the summit of pure Māyā.

Having visualized the self as a *vijñānakevala* possessing knowledge and action obstructed by *āṇava* [impurity], and being bound by the fetters (*pāśa*) of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*, one proceeds with the *vāmā* [power],
separates [the self] from the *jyeṣṭhā* [power], draws it out from the fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the *raudrī* [power], and establishes it within one's own self.

Having projected the consciousness of the disciple onto the cord of the noose (*pāśasūtra*) for the sake of stabilizing the self, one should offer five oblations with the root mantra. Then, for the removal of the disciple's defects, one should place the *arghya* water—which consists of drops of nectar—upon the disciple’s head with the ring finger using the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.
Having gratified Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara with ten oblations each and having dismissed them, one should offer the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Thereafter, [one recites] *hāṃ hrūṃ*.

Having performed the conjunction of the pure and the impure by uttering the short and long [vowels] with "Hyaiṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the bonds of the Vidyā-kalā and the Śānti-kalā," one should offer five oblations with the root mantra for its stabilization. Thus ends the purification of the Vidyā-kalā.
(Śāntikalā-śuddhiḥ) Then, having visualized the noose of the Śāntikalā as before, containing within it the five paths, [utter] *hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ*.

Having performed the striking (*tāḍana*) and piercing (*bhedana*) in their respective places with the mantra *huṃ phaṭ* for [the Lord] who possesses the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), and the bindu, as well as for the minister (*saciva*), and for Him whose form is the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattvarūpa*) and the noose of the peaceful power (*śāntikalāpāśa*), [one recites]: *hāṃ hyaiṃ* (11th line) ...
*hāṃ heṃ hāṃ tattvabhuvanavarṇapadamantramalabaindavasacivāya ktī(strī)rūpāya*.
*Haḥ* for the noose of the *kalā* of power (*śakti-kalā-pāśāya haḥ*).

*Haḥ huṃ phaṭ namaḥ* for the one accompanied by the impurity of mantra (*mantra-mala*), the lunar point (*bindu*), and the female form (*strī-rūpa*), who is the essence of the principle of tranquility (*śānti-kalā-pāśāya*).

Having entered [with this], [one recites]: *Hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ* for the one accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), karma, and the lunar point (*bindu*).

Having performed the drawing-in of the noose with the *pūraka* (inhalation) and the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* [using the mantra]: *strīrūpatattvarūpāya śāntikalāpāśāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, [one recites]: *hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ tattvabhuvanavarṇapadamantramalakarmabaindavāyasacivastrīrūpatattvarūpāya śāntikalāpāśāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.
Having grasped the noose of the *śāntikalā* with the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā] and the *kūrca* mantra (*...*), one should say:

"Obeisance to the noose of the *śāntikalā*, which is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, and the impurities (*mala*) along with the lunar point (*bindu*), and which takes the form of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*).
Having thus deposited it into the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the *recakodbhava-mudrā* and worshipped it, one should offer the *arghya* with this [mantra] ending in *svāhā*.
For the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity,
one should offer five oblations; following that, having invoked [the deity] into the sacrificial pit with "Hāṃ, obeisance to Īśvara," and having worshipped [him],
one should offer five oblations.
"O Lord, within this domain of yours, I shall initiate one who seeks liberation;
you should be favorable toward him—thus he should inform [you]."

Having dismissed Īśvara with "Hāṃ Hyaiṃ Hāṃ," [one should worship] Vāgīśvarī with the mantra: "Obeisance to Vāgīśvarī, who is accompanied by the Tattvas, Bhuvanas, Varṇas, Padas, Mantras, Mālas, and Bindu; who is the Śāntikalā; who is the Vyāpikā-pāśa. Having thus placed the red-robed, menstruating Vāgīśvarī within the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should worship her.

Having gratified [the deity] with this mantra ending in *svāhā* and having displayed the *yonimudrā*, one should offer salutation with: *Hāṃ Hyaiṃ, namaḥ to the one who is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), and the lunar drop (*bindu*), and who pervades the noose of the *śāntikalā*.
[He is] ten-armed, five-faced, and the agitator of all wombs (*yoni*).

Having placed Vāgīśvara in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and worshipped him, having gratified him with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should contemplate Vāgīśvarī— who, according to the ripening of [the disciple's] impurities, simultaneously brings about birth in many wombs within the worlds of the Śāntikalā— and having visualized the union of the two, [one recites] *hāṃ haṃ*.
"HĀṂ HAḤ ASTRĀYA HUṂ PHAṬ"—with this, having struck the animal-consciousness residing in the state of quiescence with a flower using the *nārāca* mudrā;
"HĀṂ HAṂ HĀṂ HAḤ ASTRĀYA HUṂ PHAṬ"—with this, having pierced it; "HĀṂ HAṂ HĀṂ HAḤ HUṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ."

Having offered five oblations with "huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ namaḥ hāṃ vāmāyai namaḥ," one should place Vāmā in the sacrificial pit, worship her, and offer five oblations with "huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ namaḥ (...)māyai svāhā. Then, "huṃ" (second line).
Having gone [to the left] with the *vāmā* [mantra] by means of exhalation (*recaka*), saying "Hāṃ Haṃ Huṃ Phaṭ Hīṃ Jyeṣṭhāyai Namaḥ," one should place [the mantra] in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*),

worship it, and offer five oblations (*āhuti*) with "Hāṃ Haṃ Huṃ Phaṭ Hiṃ Jyeṣṭhāyai Svāhā. Then, having separated the consciousness of the bound soul (*paśu*) residing in the thread from Jyeṣṭhā, one says "Hāṃ Huṃ Namaḥ."

Having placed [the mantra] "Hrūṃ, obeisance to Raudrī" in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and worshipped it, and having offered five oblations with "Hāṃ Hrūṃ Namaḥ, Hrūṃ Raudryai Svāhā," one should contemplate oneself as being elevated by Raudrī— vibrant and radiant through this purification, which is the state of absolute oneness.

Having led [the consciousness] to the *dvādaśānta*, [one recites]: *huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ paśucaitanyaṃ gṛhṇāmi haḥ | huṃ phaṭ*. Having thus seized that consciousness and taken it up with the *puraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breath], having established it within one's own self and led it to one's own *dvādaśānta*, and having taken it from there and worshipped Vāmā in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), [one proceeds].

Having visualized that which is supported by it— *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ ātman, being joined for the purpose of impregnation (*garbhādhāna*) in all wombs*— [one should contemplate] within Bhuvanavāgīśvarī, who possesses the form of manifold wombs and is simultaneously divided by the distinctions of many wombs.
For the sake of accomplishing the arising of the body consisting of various forms of *bindus*, one should join [the syllables] with "HĀM HAṂ HĀM ĀTMANE NAMAḤ" and worship in the *kuṇḍa*;
then, having offered libations with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one performs the libation for the presence (*sānnidhya*) with five oblations each using the root mantra ending in *svāhā*.

Having performed five oblations with the root mantra for each of them to effect their union, one should pray: "Hauṃ! Let the simultaneous union of this soul and the subtle body be ordained. Then, [one acts] so that the animal may be born from many wombs at one and the same time.

Thinking, "I perform the *garbhādhāna*," he offers five oblations with the *hṛdaya-mantra* ending in *svāhā*. Then, visualizing, "I effect the simultaneous birth of the sacrificial animal from all wombs," he offers five [more] oblations with the *śiras-mantra* ending in *svāhā*. [Then], thinking, "I effect for the sacrificial animal simultaneously everywhere an entitlement to experience (*bhogādhikāra*) corresponding to the ripening of its *āṇava-mala*," [he performs the rite].
Having reflected thus, one should offer five oblations with the *śikhā* mantra ending in *svāhā*. Regarding this, some [say]:
"In the two [levels of] Śānti and Śāntyatīta, one becomes a partaker of enjoyment (*bhoga*). What is the use of ritual action here?"

They say that for those who have not purified their actions, the body and other factors must be understood as being in accordance with those impure actions. That is incorrect; for in all the Āgamas, and here as well, action is not taught for the Śuddhādhvan (the pure path).
For those residing on the Śuddhādhvan, such as the Vijñānakalas, [their state] follows only the ripening of the *āṇavamala* (the atomic impurity). Following that—
"Regarding the instruments, the worlds, and the enjoyments":
this has been stated in the Pauṣkara:
"The cause for the variety of karmic experience does not reside in the pure Self."
The diversity of the ripening of impurity (mala) is the cause here;
that whose ripening is most intense produces experience within the principle of experience (bhogatattva),
while the other part becomes an enjoyer of experience within the two principles known as Īśvara and Vidyā.

O Indra of the three worlds, what is the use of ritual action when enjoyment is sought according to one's desire? [The principles are] Śivatattva, that which is called Sadāśiva, the principle of Īśvara, and likewise that named Vidya.
These pure principles belong to those great-souled ones named Nandana;
they are vast and inlaid with garlands of variegated cities.
Adorned with celestial women, most wonderful enjoyments free from suffering, and with bodies,
pleasures, senses, and so forth, they were lofty and inlaid with jewels.
In this [system] as well, there are *saṃhitās* whose primary focus is time, just as in other cases; however, O best of the twice-born, the *baindava* [mantras] are not pure elsewhere,
for they function independently of ritual action and the like, according to the ripening of impurities.
It favors consciousness alone, [as it were]... |||

Then, having contemplated, "I shall simultaneously bring about the state of the enjoyer in accordance with the ripening of the *āṇava-mala* which has been associated with the soul since beginningless time," one offers five oblations with the armor-mantra (*kavaca*) ending in *svāhā*. Then,
having reflected, "I effect the separation of the bond from the *bindu*," one [offers oblations] with the root-mantra ending in *svāhā*.
Having offered five oblations for the sake of removing the impurities that constitute the channels of those whose forms are similar to the gods,

and having contemplated, "I perform the purification of the animal's channels," one should offer five oblations each with the Astra-mantra ending in *svāhā* for the purpose of purifying the *śānti-kalā*.
Having offered one hundred oblations with the *kavaca* mantra, and having offered five oblations each with the root mantra for the cessation of impurity (*mala*),

one should offer five oblations each with the root mantra during the seedless initiation (*nirbījadīkṣā*) for the obscuration of the impurity of office (*adhikāramala*). Holding the thread with the index finger and thumb, one effects the separation of the bonds (*pāśa*) by moving the thread of the bonds of the bound soul (*paśu*).

Thinking, "I shall accomplish [this]," one should offer five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*. Then, having consecrated the scissors seven times with the weapon-mantra, [one should contemplate] the female form of the principle (*tattva*), accompanied by the moon of the impurities of the principles, worlds, phonemes, words, and mantras: *hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ*.

“(…) I cut the snare of the *kalā*s, *hrūṃ haḥ*, *astrāya huṃ phaṭ*. With this [mantra], one should cut the snare with a pair of scissors. Having said, “I am crushing the snare of the bound soul (*paśu*),” [one recites]: *hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ*, [and] that which is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), impurities (*mala*), and the lunar dot (*bindu*).

"I crush the bond of the *śāntikalā* which has the form of the reality of the female principle (*strīrūpatattva*), haṃ haḥ, for the weapon, huṃ phaṭ! Having thus rubbed the bond with both hands and said, "I make the bond of the bound soul (*paśu*) circular," [he recites]: "hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ"—[the bond] which is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), and the lunar point (*bindu*), and which has the form of the reality of the female principle (*strīrūpatattva*), the bond of the *śāntikalā*.

"I form a circle, *huṃ haḥ*, for the sake of the universe, *huṃ phaṭ*. Having thus spoken, and having formed a circle [of the noose] around you, saying "I burn the noose," one places the noose at the tip of the *sruva* ladle filled with clarified butter, and recites: "Hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ, I burn the noose of the *śānti* kalā, which is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, and the impurities (*mala*), along with the lunar point (*bindu*), and which has the form of the principle of the female (*strīrūpa-tattva*)."

Having offered oblations with the mantra *huṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, one should burn [the impurities]. Then, to remove the bonds (*pāśa*) and arrows, one should offer five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*; thereafter, for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should offer eight oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, [one should worship] Īśvara in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having worshipped with the heart-mantra and having gratified [the deity] with that same mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should offer five oblations with the formula: "Hāṃ! O Śuka, accept the Lord (*īśvara*), the principle (*tattva*), the world (*bhuvana*), the phoneme (*varṇa*), the word (*pada*), the mantra, the impurity (*mala*), the moon (*bindu*), the assistant (*saciva*), the female form (*strīrūpa*), the form of the principle (*tatvarūpa*), the reality (*sadhya*), and the ego (*ahaṅkāra*)—*svāhā*! (6th line).
O Lord, O Sovereign of all principles, you must never remain as a binder within your own office toward the bound soul whose every fetter has been rendered doubtful.

Having thus informed the Lord, one should dismiss him. Then, saying "I shall perform the extraction of the bound soul (*paśu*)," and having offered five oblations with the root mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should go to the left [channel] (*vāmā*),
separate oneself from the *jyeṣṭhā* [channel], and [visualize oneself] as being situated within the body of the *bindu*, like the spotless autumnal moon.

Having extracted one's own self, which is of a throbbing form, from the sacrificial pit by means of the Raudrī [kalā] and having established it within oneself, one should project the consciousness of the disciple onto the cord of bonds (*pāśasūtra*).

Then, for the sake of stabilizing one’s own self, one should offer five oblations with the root mantra; and for the nourishment of the disciple, [one should offer] with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.

Having offered water for respectful reception (*arghya*) consisting of drops of nectar upon his head with the ring finger, and having gratified Vāgīśvarī with ten oblations each by means of Vāgīśvara, one should dismiss them and offer the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Thereafter, [one should recite]: *Hāṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the nooses of the Kalās Śāntyatīta*.

Having performed the conjunction of the pure and the impure by means of short and long utterances, one should offer five oblations with the root mantra for its stabilization. Thus ends the purification of the Śāntikalā.
The purification of the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatīta).
If there is ripening within the maṇḍala, having appropriately established oneself for enjoyment among the three principles beginning with Śuddhavidyā, one should not purify what lies above;
rather, one should visualize, as before, the bond of the *kalā* beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*) containing the five paths, [uttering] *hāṃ hauṃ*.
"To the one whose ministers are the *tattva*, the world, the phoneme, the word, the mantra, the impurity (*mala*), and the *bindu*; to the one whose form is the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*);

to the one who has transcended the fetters of the *kalā* beyond peace (*śāntyatīta-kalā-pāśa*)—salutation! Thus, at its own place, having visualized the atoms beginning with the immobile (*sthāvara*) and ending with Sadāśiva, containing the *yādi* [mantra], [one recites]:

"Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ! To the one whose ministers are the *tattva*, the world, the phoneme, the word, the mantra, the impurity (*mala*), and the *bindu*; to the one whose form is the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*)... (4th line)
Having performed the striking (*tāḍana*) and piercing (*bhedana*) at its own place with "haḥ huṃ phaṭ" for the bond of the *kalā* beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*), [one recites]: "Hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ!

To the one who is the impurity of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras; to the one whose form is feminine and whose form is the principle; to the bond of the *kalā* beyond peace—haḥ!"

Having performed the separation with *huṃ* (fifth line) and *phaṭ*, [one offers] to *hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ*, to the minister who is the essence of the principles (*tattva*), the worlds (*bhuvana*), the phonemes (*varṇa*), the words (*pada*), and the mantras (*mantra*), and who has the form of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*).
Having performed the disintegration with *haḥ huṃ phaṭ* for the bond of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*, [one recites]:

*hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ*, [obeisance] to the one who is accompanied by the *tattva*, *bhuvana*, *varṇa*, *pada*, *mantra*, and *mala* bonds, as well as the lunar dot (*bindu*), and who possesses the form of the *strī-tattva* and the *śāntyatīta-kalā*-bond: *haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.
Having performed the drawing-in of the noose with the *pūraka-aṅkuśa-mudrā* while reciting "svāhā," [one should recite]: "Hāṃ Hauṃ!

To the one accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), the worlds (*bhuvana*), the mantras (*mantra*), the impurities (*mala*), and the lunar point (*bindu*); to the one whose form is the principle of womanhood; to the noose of the *kalā* beyond tranquility (*śāntyatīta*); Haḥ Huṃ! (8th line)

With the syllable *phaṭ*, by means of the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breath], having grasped the bond of the *śāntyatīta-kalā* below the *brahmarandhra*, [one offers it] to the one who has as companions the impurities (*mala*) of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), and mantras (*mantra*), and who possesses the form of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*). (Line 9)

Having offered obeisance with "Obeisance to Śāntyatīta-kalā-pāśa," one should place [the deity] in the fire-pit using the *recaka-udbhava-mudrā* and worship it. Then, having presented the *arghya* with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should offer five oblations for the sake of invoking the presence (*sannidhāna*). Thereafter, [one offers]: *Hāṃ Sadāśivāya namaḥ*.
Having thus invoked [the deity] into the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and worshipped him, and having offered five oblations with that [mantra] ending in *svāhā*, [he should say]:
"I am initiating this seeker of liberation, who is superior even to Sadāśiva;
you, being compassionate, must be favorable toward him."

Having thus requested the command from Sadāśiva and dismissed him with *hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ*, [one should worship] Vāgīśvarī with the mantra: "Obeisance to Vāgīśvarī, who is accompanied by the Tattvas, Bhuvanas, Varṇas, Padas, Mantras, and Kalās; who is the consort of the Moon; and who pervades the bonds of the Śāntyatīta-kalā. [One should then contemplate] Vāgīśvarī as the immortal speech within the mouth.
Having placed [the deity] and worshipped him, having gratified him with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, and having displayed the *yonimudrā*,

one should [worship] Vāgīśvara in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*)— who has ten arms, five faces, who utterly agitates all wombs, and who is accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras (*mantra*), and the lunar drop (*bindu*), and who pervades the fetters (*pāśa*) of the *śāntyatīta* kalā— with the mantra: "Obeisance to Vāgīśvara, the lord of speech."

Having invoked and fully worshipped [the deity], and having gratified Vāgīśvarī with this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should contemplate her as the simultaneous progenitor of birth through many wombs; then, visualizing the union of the two, one should strike the animal-consciousness (*paśucaitanya*) residing in the Śāntyatīta level with a flower using the *nārāca-mudrā* while reciting *hāṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*. Then, [recite] *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ*.
Having offered five oblations with "Astrāya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," and having split [the bonds] with "Hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ astrāya hūṃ phaṭ," [one offers again] with "Hāṃ haṃ haḥ astrāya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā."

Having offered five oblations with "hāṃ haṃ namaḥ" and "hāṃ vāmāyai namaḥ," one should place [the deity] in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), worship it, and offer five oblations with "huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ namaḥ" and "hāṃ vāmāyai svāhā. Then, having gone [to the deity] by means of the exhalation (recaka) through Vāmā with "huṃ namaḥ," [one should utter] "hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ hiṃ."

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the crown of the head with "Jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ," and having offered five oblations with "Hāṃ Haḥ Huṃ Phaṭ Hiṃ Jyeṣṭhāyai Svāhā," one should separate the consciousness of the bound soul (*paśu*) residing in the thread from Jyeṣṭhā by reciting "Haṃ Huṃ Namaḥ."

Having placed [the mantra] *hrūṃ raudryai namaḥ* in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worshipped it, and having offered five oblations with *hāṃ hrūṃ namaḥ* and *hrūṃ raudryai svāhā*, one should extract the Self together with the sheath of the bliss of consciousness (*vijñānānanda-kośa*) by means of Raudrī, lead it to the *dvādaśānta*, and [recite]: *hrūṃ hāṃ hāṃ huṃ paśucaitanyaṃ gṛhṇāmi haḥ huṃ phaṭ*. And that...
Having grasped consciousness, having taken it up through the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [breath], having established it within one's own self, having led it to one's own *dvādaśānta*,
and having drawn it from there, first [place it] in the *kuṇḍa*.

Or else, having worshipped and meditated upon that which rests therein, [one recites]: "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ! O Self, you who are engaged in placing the fragrance [of consciousness] within the remaining wombs in accordance with the ripening of impurities in the worlds of the Kalās beyond tranquility (*śāntyatīta*), [reside] in the Vāgīśvarī of the worlds who possesses the forms of manifold wombs—[a goddess] who, though undivided, simultaneously manifests the distinctions of many wombs. (106a, first line)
For the sake of accomplishing the arising of various forms, having joined [the syllables] *haṃ hāṃ ātmane namaḥ* and worshipped in the *kuṇḍa*,

one should satisfy [the deity] with this mantra ending in *svāhā*. Having performed the propitiation for the presence (*sānnidhya*) with five oblations each using the root mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should offer five oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of their union.

One should pray, "May union with all [beings] be effected for him simultaneously. Then, having discerned, "I perform the conception of the sacrificial animal (*paśu*) in many wombs at one time," one should offer five oblations with the *hṛdaya-mantra* ending in *svāhā*, while visualizing the simultaneous birth of the animal from all wombs; then, having offered five oblations with the *śiras-mantra* ending in *svāhā*, [one effects] the simultaneous [birth] of the animal.
Thinking, "I shall exercise authority everywhere," and having offered five oblations with the *śikhā* mantra ending in *svāhā*,
he should contemplate: "I bring about enjoyment simultaneously, in accordance with the ripening of the impurities of the bound soul's beginningless connection."

Having offered five oblations with the armor mantra (*kavaca*) ending in *svāhā*, and having contemplated, "I am effecting the separation of the bindu of the sacrificial animal (*paśu*)," one should offer five oblations with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) ending in *svāhā*. Then, having meditated, "I am performing the purification of the channels (*srotas*) of the sacrificial animal for the purpose of removing the body and other factors that constitute those channels which are identical in form to the bindu," [one proceeds].
Having offered five oblations each with the Astra-mantra ending in *svāhā*, and having offered five oblations with the Hṛdaya-mantra ending in *svāhā* for the purification of the tattvas,

one should offer one hundred oblations with the Mūla-mantra ending in *svāhā* for the purpose of bringing [the deity] under control and causing [the impurity] to depart; [this concerns] the impurity residing in the bones.

Having said, "I shall accomplish cessation," Śiva should offer five oblations; then, for the removal of the disciple's impurity pertaining to his spiritual office (*adhikāra-mala*), he should offer five oblations with the root mantra. Then, taking hold of the thread with the index finger and thumb, and contemplating, "I shall effect the separation of the bound soul (*paśu*) by moving the thread of bonds," he should utter *huṃ*.

One should offer five oblations with the Astra-mantra ending in *phaṭ*. Then, having consecrated the scissors (*kartarī*) seven times with the Astra-mantra— [reciting] *hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ*— [one should employ it] against the bond of the *kalā* called Śāntyatīta, which consists of the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), and the lunar point (*bindu*), and which takes the form of the female principle (*strīrūpa-tattva*).
"I cut! *Hrūṃ Haḥ! Astrāya Hūṃ Phaṭ!* With these words, one should cut the noose with a pair of scissors, saying, "I crush the noose of the bound soul (*paśu*).

Then, [one should recite]: *Hauṃ Hāṃ*, [the reality] accompanied by the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, impurities (*mala*), and the lunar dot (*bindu*), having the form of the feminine principle (*strīrūpatattva*).

With the mantra *śāntyatītakalāpāśaṃ mardayāmi huṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, [one strikes] with both hands. Having wiped away the noose, one says, "I round out the noose of the bound soul (*paśu*)," and recites *hāṃ hauṃ hauṃ*.

I form into a circle the noose, which has as its companions the principles (*tattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), phonemes (*varṇa*), words (*pada*), mantras, and the *mala* along with the lunar point (*bindu*), which takes the form of the female principle (*strītattva*) and is bound by the fetter of the *kalā* beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*); *huṃ haḥ*.
Having thus formed the noose into a circle with both hands using the mantra *astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, one says: "I burn the foot of the bound soul (*paśu*)."

Having placed the noose at the tip of the *sruva* ladle filled with clarified butter, one should consume it and then burn it with the mantra: *hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ tatvabhuvanavarṇapadamantramalabaindavīsacivaṃ strīrūpatatvarūpaṃ śāntyatītakalāpāśaṃ dahāmi hrūṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*. Thus, having consumed it, one should burn it.

Then, for the removal of the predominance of impurity (*mala*), one should offer five oblations with the *astra-mantra* ending in *huṃ phaṭ*; thereafter, for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should offer eight oblations with the *astra-mantra* ending in *svāhā*. Then, having worshipped Sadāśiva in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with the *hṛdaya-mantra* and gratified him with that same mantra ending in *svāhā*, [one should worship] Hāṃ Sadāśiva-tattva-bhuvana-varma-pada-mantra-mala-vaindava-sacivau.
