in a pavilion constructed with decorations such as arches (*toraṇa*) as previously described, having fashioned a square sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) measuring one cubit (*kara*) in size and having a single rim (*mekhalā*) six finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) high,
one should prepare a sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) measuring one cubit and six finger-breadths high in its northwestern corner.

Having constructed a funeral pit (*citākhā*) in the south-eastern direction, measuring four cubits from east to west and two cubits in width, with a depth of either eight or six finger-breadths, and having also prepared an altar (*vedi*) in the north-eastern direction for the purpose of the seat of the *astravardhanī* vessel;

Having completed all this, one should smear [the area] with cow dung. One should prepare a sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) to the south; some maintain that the site for the funeral pyre (*citāghāta*) may be located elsewhere.
(The sequence of worship of the pavilion).
Then the Guru, having bathed and performed the ritual integration (*sakaḷīkṛtya*), taking up the *vardhanī* vessel filled with water while observing silence—(third line).

Having performed the circumambulation counter-clockwise around the edge of the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*), one should sit upon a seat of *kuśa* grass consecrated with the *astra-mantra*, facing north.
Having expelled the obstacles with the *pāśupatāstra* and purified the palms by placing them back-to-back with the *astra-mantra*, one should consecrate them as nectar (*amṛtīkṛta*).

Then, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the four [mantras] beginning with the Root-mantra (*mūla*) on the palms, and having applied the *sadyojāta* and other mantras in sequence starting from the little finger and ending with the thumb, [one should proceed].
Having consecrated [the deity] by means of the *saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā] according to the sequence from end to beginning,
having veiled [it] counter-clockwise with the *kavaca*, and having rendered it supreme through the process of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*),
one who has performed the purification of the body should place the form of the *āna* in the heart, and [place] the *sandhyā* and so forth on the feet, private parts, heart, mouth, and head.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the Brahmans, and having performed the placement of the *vidyā*, the body, the eyes, and the root-mantras in the locations from the heart to the ends of the hands, and having placed the heart-mantras and the others in those places; then, preceded by three claps (*tāla*), having performed the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), one should display the great mudrā (*mahāmudrā*) with the root-mantra. Thereafter, [one should perform] the purification of the place where the internal sacrifice, oblation, and meditation have been performed.

Having performed [the preliminary rites], having purified the substances with water from the weapon-mantra recited seven times, having prepared the special *arghya* offering with the *saṃhitā* beginning with *sadyojāta*, having sprinkled the substances, performed self-worship (*ātmapūjā*), and carried out the purification of the mantras, regarding the matter of the purification of the paths (*adhvaśuddhi*):

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) upon one’s own body in the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), beginning with the *kalās* such as *nivṛtti*, one should place the limbs of Brahmā and Śiva. Then, having worshipped the Hand of Śiva (*śivahasta*) in the order of withdrawal and placed it upon one’s own head, one should remember Śiva and [apply] the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) in the order of withdrawal.

(9th line) Having performed the rites, having sprinkled [the site], having consecrated it with the purificatory rites up to the crossroads, and having scattered *kuśa* grass, ashes, sesame seeds, and so forth with the *astra-mantra*,
one should gather the *kuśa* grass and the *kūrca* bundle for the seat of the *vardhanī* vessel upon the altar in the northeast corner; then, into the *vardhanī*— (10th line)

In the southern *nāḍī* of the *vūribhūritā*, having worshipped the *Pāśupata-astra* as previously described and visualized the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*) with all remaining obstacles removed by its splendors, [one should proceed] with the pitchers situated in the directions beginning with the northeast (*īśāna*).

One should worship the weapons of the world-protectors, such as the trident and others. Then, having performed the inspection of the site by means of a stream of water from the weapon-mantra in a counter-clockwise direction, and having established the *vardhanī* vessel there, one should worship the weapon-mantra.

Having worshipped the weapons and the limbs of the weapons in reverse order on the movable seat, and having addressed [the deity] with the words, "O, O, protect this place until the completion of the rite," one should not perform [the ritual] ending at the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*). Then, in this manner, upon the sacrificial mound itself, which has been adorned with sesame seeds and *darbha* grass—
Upon a lotus made of sesame seeds and unbroken rice grains, adorned with sacred ash and parched grain, |||
Alternatively, having placed [the deity] sevenfold within a jar endowed with all splendors,
one should perform the protection over the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) using *kuśa* grass, ashes, and sesame seeds.
Having worshipped the gatekeepers and others there with the Astra-mantra and the Hṛdaya-mantra,
one should worship Ādhāraśakti and Ananta in the center— either upon sesame seeds and unbroken rice (akṣata) and ashes, or upon a simple lotus—
and then worship Aiśvarya, Vairāgya, Jñāna, and Dharma in the corners starting from the northeast (īśāna) and ending at the southeast (vahni).
Having worshipped Anaiśvarya, Avairāgya, and Ajñāna in the directions starting from the north and ending at the east; having worshipped the upper and lower petals in the corners of Īśāna and Nirṛti;
and having worshipped the powers beginning with Manonmanī and ending with Vāmā upon the eight filaments starting from Īśāna and ending at the east in the pericarp—(line 7).
In the center of the pericarp, at the tip of the pericarp, at the tips of the filaments, and at the tips of the petals, one should worship, in due order,
the mandalas of Śakti, Fire, Moon, and Sun; and having worshipped them, one should worship the Śivāsana, the Śivamūrti, and the Vidyādeha.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of Sadyojāta and the others from the feet to the top of the head, one should place the eyes of the body of the Vidyā. Regarding the purification of the paths (*adhva-śuddhi*), one should place the *kalās* beginning with Nivṛtti starting from the feet. Having invoked Śiva by means of the root-mantra of the body, one should perform the rites of installation (*sthāpana*) and the other offerings as before.

Having worshipped with the *sadyojāta* and other mantras, and having worshipped the limbs of dissolution (*layāṅga*) and offered prayers, one should worship the limbs of enjoyment (*bhogāṅga*) in the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*).
(The procedure for the fire-rite.)

Thereafter, having gone to the vicinity of the *kuṇḍa* and sat down, one should consecrate [the fire] with the four purificatory rites ending with *nirīkṣaṇa*. Having offered a seat with the mantra "Obeisance to Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa" and worshipped them, one should contemplate their union.
Then, having circumambulated the fire—consecrated by *nirīkṣaṇa* and the other rites—three times counter-clockwise, one should cast it into the womb of Vāgīśī, [uttering] "Hāṃ. (119a)
[First line:

Homage to the seed-syllable of Śiva (*śivabīja*). Then, having performed the purification and sipping of water (*śaucācamana*), and having performed the purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*) beginning with conception (*garbhādhāna*) as if they were obligatory (*nityavat*), one should spread *darbha* grass upon the girdles (*mekhalā*) in reverse order.

Having placed the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) and the seat-grass (*viṣṭara*) with their tips pointing westward and arranged counter-clockwise, one should offer five fuel-sticks (*samidh*) with the mantra "haḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā" for the removal of saliva.
Then, in the northern, southern, southern, western, and eastern directions among the enclosing sticks, [one should worship] Ananta, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā.
And having worshipped [the deities] on their seats in the directions starting from Īśāna and ending with the East— namely, Īśāna, Kubera, Vāyu, Varuṇa, Nirṛti, Yama, Agni, Indra, and Nairṛta—
and having worshipped Viṣṇu in the northeast and Brahmā [in the southeast], one should cause them to hear the command of Śiva: "Protect the infant fire."

Having consecrated the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles with the four purificatory rites beginning with inspection (*nirīkṣaṇa*), having sprinkled them with the *astra-mantra* and rotated them three times clockwise, and having consecrated them as before, one should perform the ritual up to the end of the offering of the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*)— including the purification of the clarified butter (*ājya-saṃskāra*), the sprinkling on the mouth (*vaktrābhighāra*), the joining of the mouths (*vaktra-sandhāna*),

the unification of the mouths (*vaktra-ekīkaraṇa*), the naming (*nāmakaraṇa*), and the dismissal of the Goddess of Speech (*vāgīśī*) and the Lord of Speech (*vāgīśa*)— all according to the previous procedure, within the heart of the Fire.
On the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*), having invoked and worshipped Śiva along with his limbs (*sāṅga*) in reverse order,

omitting the mantra-satiation (*mantratarpaṇa*) and having offered the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), one should offer oblations according to one's capacity and in accordance with the substance and time for the sake of the place, time, and other factors, using the root mantra; then, having fully satiated the collection of mantras and kindled them, one should offer the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
(Vāstupūjā and so forth:

Subsequently, just as for the funeral pyre, having divided [the ground] into twenty-five squares with six lines drawn from east to west and north to south, one should provide it with bamboo and cords.

Having prepared the site there according to its proper form and meditated upon it, one should worship it; then, having adorned the five central squares with yellow powder, the four squares in the southwest with white powder,
the four squares in the southeast with red powder, the four squares in the northwest with black powder, and the four squares in the northeast with white powder.

Having adorned the four [squares], starting from the east and following the sequence of the cells, one should fill them with yellow, black, white, and red powders. Thereafter, in the center, one should offer: "Hāṃ, obeisance to the earth element; Hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā, the presiding deity of the earth element. Then: "Hāṃ, obeisance to the water element; Hāṃ, obeisance to [the deity] presiding over the water element."

"To Viṣṇu, obeisance!"—in the northwest. "Hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of fire; Hāṃ, obeisance to Rudra, the lord of the principle of fire"—in the southeast. "Hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of air; Hāṃ, obeisance to Īśvara, the lord of the principle of air"—in the northwest. (119b, 1st line)
"Hām, obeisance to the element of space; hām, obeisance to Sadāśiva, the lord of the element of space. Having thus worshipped in the northeast, [he worships] with:
"Hām, obeisance to Indra; hām, obeisance to Yama; hām, obeisance to Varuṇa; hām, obeisance to Kubera. (Second line)
Having thus worshipped in the remaining squares, one should offer a *bali* of black gram (*māṣa*) rice soaked in ghee to them. (Rituals to be performed at the site of the funeral pyre:
Then, having wiped away the *bali*, one should prepare a square mandala there with yellow powder, as in the case of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), and in its center—

Having fashioned a triangular maṇḍala from blood and flesh, one should worship by saying "Hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā" at the square, and "Hāṃ, obeisance to Kālāgnirudra" at the triangle. Then, having recited the Astra-mantra seven times over dry stakes that are rooted upward and facing downward— (Note: The text provided consists of Sanskrit fragments with interspersed English instructions for ritual performance.)

Having placed [the fires] in the directions of Agni, Īśāna, Anila, and Rakṣas, one should bind them with a red thread while moving counter-clockwise (apasavya). Then, having filled the funeral pyre with fuel sticks smeared with sandalwood and other substances consecrated by the *yā o jñikā* mantra, one should worship it with the *astra-mantra*.

Having covered [the body] with a cloth whose ends point southward, having worshipped with "Hāṃ, obeisance to the funeral pyre" (hāṃ citāyai namaḥ), and having performed protection in reverse order using the *astra-mantra* ending in *huṃ phaṭ* along with ashes and *darbha* grass, one should invoke the Lord of the Site (*vāstupati*) for the sake of the pyre and the deities residing in the site into one's own navel.
One should satisfy [the deity].
(The bathing of the deceased, etc.
Then, having washed Śiva with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and with water mixed with earth and cow dung, and having bathed him with the *śivāmbhas* while reciting the *astra-mantra*.
Having dusted him with ashes using the *sandhyā* mantras and others in the sequence beginning with the feet,

having changed his garments for a loincloth and a new cloth, and having given the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*) to one regardless of previous caste, he should seat him on a seat of *kuśa* grass upon which the *praṇava* has been placed, at the southern side of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).
(The Procedure for the Ritual Duties Regarding a Body Constructed from Kuśa Grass):
In this interval, due to the deficiency of the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) and so forth,

or because of death in another land, one who at that time was joined with an untimely death (*durmaraṇa*) due to the absence of funeral rites (*antyeṣṭi*) in the presence of a *preta*— [End of fragment]

Furthermore, since it is prescribed that the funeral rites (*antyeṣṭi*) should be performed preceded by expiation after the aforementioned interval of time has passed, one should perform the installation (*nyāsa*) of the thirty-six principles along with their presiding deities (*sādhipa*) and so forth, within the body of the deceased fashioned from *kuśa* grass and other materials during the initiation of the dead (*mṛtakadīkṣā*).
(Union with the World of Śiva, etc. Then,
having consecrated the deceased body— or a body fashioned from *kuśa* grass and other materials— by means of the fourfold [rites] beginning with "beholding" (*nirīkṣaṇa*),
one should purify the body through *bhūtaśuddhi*, *dhāraṇā*, and so forth.

Having purified and flooded [the seat] with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, and having worshipped the seat in the heart, [one recites]: "haṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ [Name]"— for although the self is all-pervasive, movement to and fro occurs because it is delimited by the subtle body.

"Salutation to the Self of Consciousness. When prārabdha-karma has been destroyed through the application of the Great Net (*mahājāla*), because of any deficiency in the conduct of the observances (*samaya*) such as the *caryā*, the attainment of states such as *śivasālokya* would be impossible; [the soul remains] like a stone within the body of the eightfold city (*puryaṣṭaka*).
Having grasped the self, which is devoid of knowledge and remains alone, with the *saṃhārakamudrā* and the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*,

one should place it within one's own heart by means of inhalation (*pūraka*), rest there during retention (*kumbhaka*), and then, by exhalation (*recaka*), deposit it upon the lotus of the corpse’s heart.

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and contemplated the three fetters of impurity and so forth, one should [invoke] the Brahmās, beginning with Sadyojāta, in the sequence starting from the feet.

Having projected the *vidyādeha* (body of knowledge), and for the purpose of purifying the paths (*adhvaśuddhi*), having projected the *kalās*— Nivṛtti and the others— at the knees, navel, throat, eyebrows, and the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*), and having projected the limbs of Śiva as the presiding deities, one should offer a hundred oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*) for the sake of invoking the presence of consciousness (*caitanya*).
Then, for the purpose of joining the channels (*nāḍī*) and for their proximity, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. Thereafter,

having extracted the consciousness residing in the corpse's body as before and brought it into one's own heart, and having meditated on the seven equinoxes (*viṣuva*), one should worship it in the world of Śiva with a full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*).
Having united Śiva residing on the sacrificial mound with Śiva residing in the fire,

one should offer oblations ending with the *pūrṇāhuti* one hundred and eight times using the root mantra, and then dismiss Śiva. Thereafter, having placed the corpse upon the funeral pyre, [one should cremate it] with the Śiva-fire.

Having kindled [the fire], one should perform the other rites as will be described hereafter. (Regarding the special funeral rite: Having performed everything for the initiate of distinction (*viśiṣṭasamayin*) as previously stated, up until the joining of the channels (*nāḍīsandhāna*) with the fire...

Having performed everything, having worshipped Vāgīśī and Vāgīśa within the lotus of the heart of the fire (*agnihṛdayapatra*), and having offered three oblations to each for the sake of their presence, one should contemplate them as united; then, having sprinkled the corpse with the Astra-mantra,
and having struck it at the region of the heart with the *sapuṣpanārāca-mudrā* while reciting "Haḥ Huṃ Phaṭ," [one should do so] by means of one's own exhalation (*recaka*).
Having entered his body with the syllable *huṃ*, and having separated [the soul] from it using the *jyeṣṭhā* [mudrā] while reciting *huṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ hrūṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*,

and then [reciting] *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svadhāhaḥ* with the goad-mudrā (*aṅkuśamudrā*), one should lead that life-force (*jīva*), which is in the form of a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, to the end of the twelve [fingers].

Having reflected, one should gather [the deity] with the *saṃhāramudrā* while reciting one’s own mantra ending in *namaḥ*; having drawn it in through the process of inhalation (*pūraka*), one should establish it within one’s own heart. Then, performing retention (*kumbhaka*) while recollecting the root mantra, one should lead [the deity] to the *dvādaśānta* by means of one’s own mantra through the sequential abandonment of the causal deities beginning with Brahmā; having gathered it there, one should draw it out through one’s own channel (*nāḍī*).
Having visualized the union of the two purifiers (*pavitra*),
joined with Vāgīśvarī by means of the *vāmaja-udbhava-mudrā* and one's own mantra, one should offer oblations—
one hundred, one thousand, or half— that number— into oneself with the root mantra and the *pūrṇāhuti*.

Having joined Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara near Śiva, who presides over the station of Īśvara, and having gratified and dismissed them, one should offer one hundred and eight oblations with the Astra-mantra for the sake of expiation; then, having united the Lord of the Altar (Sthaṇḍileśa) with the fire residing within [the deity], one should dismiss Śiva. Thereafter, having placed the corpse on the funeral pyre with its head facing south...

Having covered [the vessel] with a cloth and having covered it with fuel-sticks, and having kindled the Śiva-fire produced from within the hearth, one should place clarified butter, honey, and milk upon the head [of the fire].
Having lifted up the full *sruva* and *sruc* ladles, one should utter this speech while they are thus full:
"O Agni, you are the southern time; accept this great oblation, born of the sacred mantra, offered by Śāṇḍilī at the very moment ordained by Time. Thus [he spoke].

Then, having placed the *astravardhanī* pitcher upon his left shoulder with its stream unbroken, turning it away from him and moving counter-clockwise, he should lower it face-down at its own place; then, without looking back, having gone to the water reservoir and bathed, [he stands] on the bank.
Having spread out *kuśa* grass, one should offer three handfuls of water-libations (*añjali*), reciting: "Hāṃ! O Pure One, become Skanda, Svadhā! Hāṃ!
O Pure-Souled One, become Caṇḍa, Svadhā! Hāṃ! O Pure-Souled One, become Gaṇādhīśa, Svadhā!
Thus one should mutter [this] for the purpose of the expiation of the re-bathing.

Now follows the final *iṣṭi* (sacrifice) accompanied by purification (*śuddhasahitāntyeṣṭi*). Having performed the ritual up to the joining of the channels (*nāḍīsandhāna*) as before, one should take the cord of bonds (*pāśasūtra*), which has been tripled and then tripled again (i.e., ninefold), along with the scissors; it must be washed with the *astra-mantra*, sprinkled with water, and concealed with the *kavaca-mantra*. (8th line)
Having accomplished this and informed Śiva, one should bind [the thread] from the big toe up to the crest-lock with the root mantra; then, within that [thread] which consists of the *suṣumnā*,
one should say "Laṃ, obeisance to the *suṣumnā*," and thus grasp the *suṣumnā* by means of the unification of the *iḍā* and *piṅgalā*.
Having joined [the thread] with the *sūtra*, worshipped it, and veiled it, one should offer three oblations for its presence (*sannidhāna*). Then,
having worshipped the *śakti* mantra on the head of the disciple, taken [the thread], and placed it upon the *sūtra*, one should worship it, veil it,
and offer three oblations for its presence.

Having sprinkled the disciple with the *astra-mantra* (*haḥ huṃ phaṭ*), one should withdraw [the disciple's consciousness] into one's own heart with a flower. Then, emerging through one's own exhalation (*recaka*) accompanied by the syllable *huṃ*, and entering the disciple's heart through his left channel (*vāmanāḍī*) via inhalation (*pūraka*), one should contemplate the consciousness situated there within the seed-syllable *haṃ*. Then, with the mantra *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, one should separate it from the *jyeṣṭhā* [channel].
Having drawn [the soul] out with the mantra "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Svāhā" and the goad mudrā,

and having led it to the dvādaśānta, one should contemplate the individual soul (jīva) in the form of the bindu at the tip of the three qualities; then, grasping it with the self-mantra and the withdrawal mudrā.

Having established [the deity] in one's own heart by means of *pūraka* (inhalation), and having performed *kumbhaka* (retention) while recollecting the root mantra, one should lead [the deity] to the *dvādaśānta* (the end of the twelve finger-breadths) by means of the *ātman-mantra*, following the sequence of abandoning the causal deities beginning with Brahmā. Having withdrawn [the deity] there, one should bring it back to the middle of the eyebrows through the process of emanation (*sṛṣṭi*). Then, expelling [it] through the right channel of oneself by means of *recaka* (exhalation), one should join it to the thread using that same [mantra] ending with *namaḥ*.
Having enveloped the pervasive [deity] with the *saṃbhāvya* mantra and brought it into proximity,

one should offer three oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*). Then, having taken up the three bonds of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*), and having joined them, [one offers to] the presiding deity of the bonds.

Having taken up the mantra "Salutation to Śiva-Śakti," having joined it with that which resides in the thread, having worshipped it, and having offered three oblations for the purpose of invoking its presence, one should contemplate the Nivṛtti-kalā, which contains the principles (tattvas) and so forth, while reciting "hlāṃ, salutation to the Nivṛtti-kalā."

Reciting "hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai huṃ phaṭ," one strikes with a flower below the knee; then, having gathered it with the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, one places it on the thread at the location of Nivṛtti, reciting "hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai namaḥ. (Line 7)

Having joined [the mantras] and performed worship, one should offer three *sannidhāna* oblations. Then, having visualized the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*— which contains the *tattva*s and other elements— with the mantra "hlīṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai namaḥ," and having struck below the navel with "huṃ phaṭ" and seized [the deity],...

Having established [the deity] in the location of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* according to the *Namonta-sūtra*, and having worshipped [him], one should offer three *sannidhāna* oblations. Having visualized the *vidyā-kalā*— which contains the *tattva*s and other elements— with the mantra "Hrūṃ, obeisance to the *vidyā-kalā*," one should [offer oblations] below the throat with the mantra ending in "Huṃ Phaṭ."

Having struck [the thread] and grasped it with the mantra ending in *namaḥ*, one should place that thread in its proper position, worship it, and offer three oblations for the sake of its presence, saying: *hyaiṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ*. Then, having visualized the *śāntikalā* containing the *tattva*s and so forth, one should utter *huṃ*.

Having struck below the space between the eyebrows with the mantra ending in *phaṭ*, and having grasped [the thread] with the mantra ending in *namaḥ*, one should place the thread in that position and offer three oblations for its presence. Then, having visualized the Śāntyatītā-kalā, which contains the principles (*tattva*) and so forth, with the mantra *hauṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ*, [one should strike] below the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) with the mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*.
Having struck [the thread] and grasped it with the mantra ending in *namaḥ*, one should join it to the thread in the station beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*),
worship it, and offer three oblations for its presence (*sannidhāna*).

(Second line) Likewise, having recollected the remaining [elements], including the seeds of the conventional conduct regarding caste, lifespan, and experience, ending with the name of the station of the *kalā*s.

Having gratified [the deity] in sequence with three oblations ending in *svāhā*, and having performed the purification (*dīvana*) in the same order with the mantra *hūṃ hlāṃ hūṃ nivṛttikalāyai huṃ phaṭ*, one should smear the locations of the *kalās* with saffron and other substances, worship Śiva together with his limbs (*sāṅga*) therein, and [recite] *haḥ huṃ*.

Having touched the thread below the knee with "Phaṭ," having struck it with the Nārāca-mudrā, and having entered by means of the *kalā*-mantra ending in "Namaḥ," one takes hold of it, offers three oblations, and ties a knot in the thread with: "Hauṃ hlāṃ hauṃ!
O Blessed One, bind, bind the noose of the *nivṛtti-kalā* which pervades impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), the principle of *māyā*, the worlds, and so forth; Huṃ Phaṭ!"
One should perform [this].

Then, having struck the navel with the Astra-mantra, and having entered with "Hlīṃ, obeisance to the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā," one should take hold [of it] and offer an oblation ending in Svāhā; [then recite]: "Hauṃ Hlīṃ Hauṃ, O Lord, the bond of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā."
(6th line) One should tie a knot in the thread with the mantra: *malakarma māyā-tattva-bhuvana-ādi-vyāpakaṃ bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ*.

Afterwards, having struck it at the throat with the Astra-mantra (*hūṃ phaṭ*) and performed the entry and grasping with *hūṃ phaṭ ākāśayai namaḥ*, [one should conclude] with the end of the *svāhā* mantra.
Having offered three oblations with the mantra *hauṃ hrūṃ hauṃ bhagavan vidyākalāpāśaṃ malakarmamāyātatvabhuvanādivyāpakaṃ bandhabandha huṃ phaṭ*, one should tie a knot in the thread.
Thereafter, having struck the forehead region with the Flower-Arrow (*puṣpāstra*), one should offer: *hyaiṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ*.

(7th line) Thus. Having entered and taken [the thread], one should offer three oblations ending with *svāhā*, and then form a knot in the thread while reciting: *hauṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ bhagavan śāntikalāpāśaṃ tattvabhuvanādivyāpaka bandha-bandha huṃ phaṭ*. Then (8th line).

Having struck [the head] with a flower while reciting "HAḤ HUṂ PHAṬ" on the head, and having performed the entry and grasping with "HAUṂ ŚĀNTYATĪTAKALĀKHYE NAMAḤ," one should offer three oblations ending in SVĀHĀ, [reciting]: "HAUṂ, O Blessed One, the noose of the Śāntyatīta-kalā,
which pervades the principles (tattva), worlds (bhuvana), and so forth."

Having tied a knot in the thread with the mantra *bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ*, one should perform a hundred oblations (*homa*) with the root mantra for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*). Then, having worshipped the Support-Power (*ādhāra-śakti*) in the fire and offered three oblations, one should visualize the digit of Cessation (*nivṛtti-kalā*) in the body of the disciple at the location below the knees upon the thread.
(Purification of the Nivṛtti-kalā):
Thereafter—hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the bond of the Nivṛtti-kalā; hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Earth-tattva;
hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ. (122a, first line)

Salutation to the one hundred and eight worlds beginning with Kālāgni and ending with Bhadrakālī. Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the syllable Kṣa. Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, salutation to those seized from the waking state born of the aggregate of the letter A. Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the twenty-eight stations beginning with Oṃkāra and ending with Bhavānta. Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ.
Salutation with the Heart and Sadyojāta mantras. Homage to the seed-syllable *hauṃ hāṃ hlāṃ*. Homage to the sense-object of fragrance (*gandha-viṣaya*) with *hāṃ hlāṃ*.
*Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ*. (Third line)

Salutation to the five qualities beginning with fragrance and ending with sound. Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the yellow, four-cornered earth mandala, marked by a vajra and measuring one hundred crore yojanas; Hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the cause. (4th line)

Having worshipped those [limbs] which have the luster of gold, and having taken them up through the processes of filling (*pūraka*) and withdrawal (*saṃhāra*), one should join them to the thread extending from the knees to the big toes of the feet;
having worshipped them there, restrained them, and enveloped them, and having likewise worshipped them in the fire, one should offer five oblations for the sake of their presence (*sannidhāna*).

Then, having contemplated the three bonds (*pāśatraya*)—which consist of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and the substrate (*ādhāra*), and which produce the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), the body of experience (*bhoga-śarīra*), and so forth—one should utter "Hāṃ."

Having invoked Brahmā with "Obeisance to Brahmā," worshipped him, offered three oblations, and made a formal request, one should conceive of the entire womb within that *kalā*. Then, having invoked, worshipped, and brought into proximity the pervasive Vāgīśvarī,
and likewise having worshipped Vāgīśvara, meditated upon them as before, and performed invocation and worship, one should offer the oblation for their presence (*sannidhāna*).

Having said, "May you remain present for the sake of favoring the sacrificial animal," and having sprinkled the disciple with the Astra-mantra, he should strike the region of the heart with a flower while reciting *haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, and [expel the impurities] from that place by means of exhalation (*recaka*) together with the syllable *huṃ*.

Having entered with "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Haḥ Huṃ Phaṭ," having separated [the deity] with the Jyeṣṭhā [finger], and having grasped [it] with the Aṅkuśa-mudrā while reciting "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Svāhā," one should establish [the deity] in one's own heart through inhalation (*pūraka*), perform breath-retention (*kumbhaka*),
and while recollecting the root mantra, [recite] "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ."

Saying "Salutation to the Self" (*ātmane namaḥ*), one should lead [the consciousness] to the *dvādaśānta* by means of the sequential abandonment of the causal deities beginning with Brahmā; having grasped it and visualized the union of the parents, one should perform the rite according to the specific ritual requirement, reciting: "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the Self," while employing the *utbhavamudrā* with the left hand.
Having simultaneously established union with the Self in the form of manifold individual manifestations within all wombs, and having worshipped with the root mantra and offered three oblations,
one should inform [the deity] and offer three oblations with the root mantra for the completion of all embryos; then,
having made the prayer and conceived the simultaneous growth of all bodies for the sake of the authority over enjoyment—
Having meditated upon [the self] as the recipient of the portion of previously accumulated karma within the bodies of all wombs,

and having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a formal request, one should contemplate that the state of being an enjoyer— manifesting in various forms according to the distinctions of place, time, body, and object— is not the self.

Having reflected upon experience consisting of the sensations of pleasure and pain, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and make a formal request. At this juncture, in the case of initiation for the deceased, one should perform the sixteen purificatory rites beginning with conception (*garbhādhāna*) and the preceding stages of life, offering oblations as previously described.
Having contemplated absorption (*laya*), which consists of supreme delight in objects of enjoyment, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and make a formal request; then,
for the purification of the streams [of the senses], one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the purification of the flow that initiates the activity of *māyā*.

Having made a request for the purification of the reality of cessation (*nivṛtti-tattva-śuddhi*), one should offer three oblations with the heart-mantra. Then, for the sake of expiation and atonement, one should offer one hundred oblations with the root-mantra while reciting the heart-mantra; having made a formal petition and envisioned the severance of the bonds of *māyā*, one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra. Finally, for the purpose of removing the obscuration of impurity (*malatirodhāna*), one should offer one hundred oblations with the root-mantra and resolve upon the distinction from that which is accompanied by impurity.
One should again offer three oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, contemplating the disjunction of the karma residing in the worlds of the *nivṛtti-kalā* in its manifest form;
having offered three oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, [one should pray]:
"O Blessed One, effect the disjunction of this soul's triple bond consisting of the impurity of *māyā*, the *nivṛtti-kalā*, and the nature of karma."

One should request, "Do so. Thereafter, having cut the bond of the *nivṛtti-kalā* with the sound "haḥ huṃ phaṭ" using a knife consecrated seven times with the *astra-mantra*, and having wiped it with the *astra-mantra*,
rolled it into a ball, and placed it in a *sruk* ladle filled with ghee, one should [offer] it together with the clarified butter using that same mantra.

Having offered [the oblation], one should burn [the effigy]. O Blessed One, having requested, "Cut the bonds of the collection of the cessation of this self," and having offered five oblations with the mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ* for the removal of the noose and the goad,
one should offer eight oblations with the *astra-mantra* for the sake of atonement.

Having conceived the oneness of consciousness even when the entire body has perished, one should invoke Brahmā, worship him, and offer three oblations. Then, for the sake of purifying the *puryaṣṭaka*, one should offer three oblations with the mantra: "Hāṃ, O Brahmā, accept sound and touch, along with dryness, Svāhā! Thereafter, one should address him: "O Brahmā, you have not [attained] the stainless state of this element."
"The obstruction must be established; such is the supreme command of the Lord.

Having dismissed Brahmā and having contemplated the Self as resembling the lunar orb when a portion of it has been released by Rāhu—freed from the net of the kalās of Nivṛtti—for the sake of extraction:

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and preceded by a formal petition, one should extract the self from the fire as the essence of Raudrī with the mantra "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Ātmane Namaḥ. Then, by means of the left nostril and inhalation, one should [visualize] the self as resembling the lunar orb partially released from Rāhu, consisting of the *nivṛtti-kalā*. One's own...

Having brought [the deity] into the heart with the *recaka* breath and the *udbhavamudrā*, having joined it to the thread-body of the disciple and worshipped it, one should give a drop of *arghya* water upon the head with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* for the purpose of nourishment (*āpyāyana*). Then, for the sake of stabilization (*sthirīkaraṇa*), one should offer an oblation (*āhuti*) with the root mantra, worship the two parents, satisfy them with three oblations, and after honoring them, dismiss them; finally, one should offer the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.
Thus concludes the purification of the kalā of nivṛtti.
(The Purification of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā):

Thereafter, the conjunction of time should be performed; having worshipped with "hlāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the kalās of Nivṛtti and Pratiṣṭhā," and having offered three oblations, one should contemplate the pure [kalā] as dissolved into the impure, and then invoke the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā.

(5th line) Then, having projected the *ādhāraśakti* into the fire and worshipped it, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) and contemplate its pervasion within the body of the thread at the location of the *pratiṣṭhākalā*. Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the noose of the *pratiṣṭhākalā*. Hāṃ (6th line).

Hlīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the twenty-three principles beginning with Water and ending with Mind (citta). Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the fifty-six worlds beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha at the end of the syllable Oṃ. Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the twenty-three phonemes beginning with Ha and ending with A in the Suṣumnā [channel]. Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, [salutation] to those accompanied by the syllable U and the auspicious dream.

Salutation to the thirty-two syllables beginning with *Śarva* and ending with *Vyāpin*. Salutation to the two mantras of the Head (*Śira*) and Vāmadeva: *Hāṃ Hvīṃ Hiṃ Hvīṃ Hāṃ*. Salutation to the seed-syllable *Vaṃ*: *Hāṃ Hvīṃ Hāṃ Vaṃ*. Salutation to the two channels (*nāḍī*) Sumanā and Gāndhārī: *Hāṃ Hvīṃ Hāṃ*. Salutation to the two vital airs (*vāyu*) Samāna and Udāna: *Hlāṃ Hvīṃ Hāṃ*. *Hāṃ*.
Hvīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two organs of the anus and the tongue. Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the object of taste.
(9th line) Hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the qualities of taste, form, touch, and sound. Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, salutation to the white water-maṇḍala.
"Obeisance to the one whose essence is substance, who has the form of a half-moon, who measures one thousand crores of *yojanas*. Hāṃ hlīṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the cause of Viṣṇu.

Having worshipped these white [elements], having taken them up with the *pūraka* (inhalation) and the *saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā], and having joined them within the navel at the level of the knees, one should worship them.

Having extinguished [the fire], covered it, and worshipped it, one should offer five oblations for the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity. Thereafter, having visualized the three bonds (*pāśatraya*)—

consisting of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*)— which produce the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*), the body, and so forth, [one should offer] "Hāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu."
Having invoked Viṣṇu, worshipped him, offered three oblations for his presence, and made a formal request, one should conceive of the various forms and origins within that digit (kalā),
worship Vāgīśvarī who presides over it as before, and having caused her to be present, pray for her presence.

Having sprinkled the disciple with the Weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ* and struck him on the heart with a flower, one enters his body; then, having separated [the consciousness] from the body using the thumb-finger (*jyeṣṭhā*) with one's own mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*, and having drawn it out with the Hook-gesture (*aṅkuśamudrā*) ending in *svāhā*.
Having led that [consciousness] to the *dvādaśānta* and meditated upon Śiva, one should establish it within one's own heart by means of the *ātma-mantra* and the *saṃhāra-mudrā*;
then, having performed *kumbhaka*,
while recollecting the *mūla-mantra*, one should lead it to the *dvādaśānta* by means of the *ātma-mantra* through the sequential abandonment of the causal deities beginning with Brahmā.
Having drawn [the breath] through the right channel and having visualized the union of the parents,

one should effect the simultaneous union of the self with all wombs— in the form of manifold manifestations— by means of the left-hand *utbhavamudrā* and the *ātma-mantra*; then, one should worship with the root mantra (*mūla*).

Having offered three oblations for the placement of the embryo and made the request, and having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the completion of the entire embryo and made the request,

and having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the completion of the entire embryo and made the request, and having performed three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the people and made the request, [he performs] three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the office.
Having made an offering for that purpose and requested [the deity's presence], one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of enjoyment; having requested [again],
one should offer three dissolution-oblations with the root mantra.

Having requested [the purification] for the purity of the channels (*srotas*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra; having prayed for the purification of the principle of installation (*pratiṣṭhā-tattva*), one should perform three oblations with the heart mantra (*hṛdaya*). For the sake of expiation (*niṣkṛti*), having offered one hundred oblations with the root mantra together with the head mantra (*śiras*), and having made the request, [one effects] the distinction from the *māyīya* bond.
Having honored [the deity] and offered three oblations with the root mantra, and having offered one hundred oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of removing impurities (*mala*),

one should contemplate the disjunction from impurity; then, having again performed three oblations with the root mantra, one should contemplate the disjunction of the nature of action (*karman*) from the levels of *pratiṣṭhā*, *kalā*, and *bhuvana*.

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should request: "O Blessed One, effect the separation (*viśleṣa*) of the three bonds (*pāśatraya*)—namely, the impurity of *māyā*, the impurity of *kala*, and the impurity of karma—which pervade this self. Then, having recited the weapon-mantra (*astra*) seven times, one should [strike] with the knife while reciting: *hvīṃ* for the bond of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*, and *haḥ huṃ*.
Uttering "phaṭ" with its proper vowel-sound, one should sever the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* with the *astra-mantra*, wipe it away, and roll it into a circle.

Having placed it in a ladle (*sruc*) filled with clarified butter and offered it as an oblation (*homa*) with that same mantra, one should then use the sacrificial spoon (*darvī*) while saying: "O Blessed One, perform the severance of the noose of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* of this self; perform it!"
Having made the request for the cessation of the noose and the goad, and having offered five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*,
one should offer eight oblations with the weapon-mantra for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*). Then, having meditated upon the oneness of consciousness even as the entire body is being destroyed,
one should invoke and worship Viṣṇu, offer three oblations, and [recite] "Hāṃ, the dry essence of Viṣṇu" for the purification of the subtle body (*puryaṣṭaka*).
Having offered three oblations with "gṛhāṇa svāhā," he should make this request:
"O Viṣṇu, may there be well-being for the feet of this traveler as he departs."
"The negation must be established"—such is the command of the Supreme Goddess.

Thus one should dismiss Viṣṇu. Then, having contemplated oneself as being liberated from the web of the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalās, resembling the moon released from Rāhu, and having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of extraction (*uddhāra*), one should request [permission] and extract oneself from the *raudrī* fire by means of the *vāmā* [mantra].

Having brought the self, resembling the moon released from Rāhu’s mouth, into one's own heart by means of *pūraka* (inhalation), one should join it to the thread of the disciple's body by means of *recaka* (exhalation) and the *udbhava-mudrā*. Then, having worshipped it and offered a drop of *arghya* water upon the head for nourishment, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*) for the sake of stabilization.

(7th line) Having given [the offerings], having worshipped the parents, having satiated them, and having dismissed them, one should offer the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. Thus ends the purification of the *pāśa* in the *Pratiṣṭhākalāpa*.
(The purification of Vidyā and Kalā). Then follows the unification with Kalā.

Having worshipped with "Hvīṃ Hrūṃ, obeisance to Pratiṣṭhā and Vidyākalā" (the eighth line), and having offered three oblations while contemplating that the pure [element] has dissolved into the impure, one should establish Vidyākalā. Having worshipped Śakti in the fire with "Hām, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" and having offered three oblations, [one should place it] in the body of the thread at the location of Vidyākalā.

(9th line) One should observe its pervasion: *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the noose of the *vidyā-kalā*; *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the seven principles beginning with *puruṣatva* and ending with *māyā*; *hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*.

Salutation to the twenty-seven worlds beginning with Krodheśa and ending with Gopa. Hāṃ Hrūṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the seven syllables beginning with Ña and ending with Dha. Hāṃ Hrūṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the twenty-one steps beginning with food (anna) in the ether accompanied by Suṣupti and Makāra, and ending with Om. Hāṃ Hrūṃ...

(124b, 1st line) ... [to] the two terrible mantras, *namaḥ*. *Hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, *namaḥ* to the seed-syllable *ra*. *Hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, *namaḥ* to the tongue and the *pūṣan*-channel situated therein. *Hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ*, *namaḥ* to the serpent (*nāga*) and the pervasive wind (*vyāna-vāyu*). *Hāṃ hrūṃ*.
Hāṃ (second line), homage to the sense organs of the hands and eyes. Hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ, homage to the object of form. Hāṃ hrū hāṃ.

Salutation to the qualities of form, touch, and sound. Hāṃ Hrūṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the red fire-mandala, whose nature is burning, which is one's own limb, which is triangular, and which measures ten million times ten thousand yojanas; salutation to the cause of Rudra. Hāṃ Hrūṃ Hāṃ, salutation! Thus it is said.

Having worshipped those [deities] red as the sun, and having taken them up through the *pūraka* (inhalation) and *saṃhāra* (withdrawal) [breaths], one should join them to the thread extending from the heart to the navel, worship them there,
restrain them, encircle them, and worship them in the fire.

One should offer five oblations for the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity. Thereafter, having visualized the three bonds (*pāśatraya*)— consisting of impurity (*mala*), action (*karman*), and illusion (*māyā*),

which produce the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*) and the body and so forth— one should invoke Rudra with the mantra "Obeisance to Rudra" (*rudrāya namaḥ*), worship him, offer three oblations for his presence (*sannidhāna*), and having made a formal request, one should conceive of the womb (*yoni*) of manifold forms within that *kalā*.
Having worshipped Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, who pervade that [deity], as before, and having caused them to become present and prayed for their presence,
one should sprinkle the disciple with the Astra-mantra, seize him according to the previous sequence of striking and so forth, and [place him] before the two parents.
Having visualized the union by means of the *utbhava* (emergence) mudrā with the left hand and the self-mantra,

one should effect the simultaneous union of the self with all wombs (*yoni*) in the form of manifold manifestations; then, having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a formal request, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the completion of all embryos, and finally pray.

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of birth, and having made a formal request for the sake of [establishing] authority, one should contemplate the simultaneous growth of all bodies; then, having meditated upon the karma that bestows experience within all wombs, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and make a formal request.

Having reflected upon experience consisting of pleasure and pain, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and inform [the deity]. Then, having meditated on dissolution into the objects of experience in the form of supreme delight, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and inform [the deity] for the purification of the channels (*srotas*).

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a formal request for the purification of the reality of the Vidyā, one should perform three oblations with the heart-mantra for the sake of expiation.

Then, having offered one hundred oblations with the root mantra preceded by the *śikhā*-mantra, [one should pray]: "O Blessed One, having performed this expiation for myself, grant purity in all ritual actions."
Having requested [the deity] to act for the sake of loosening the noose of *māyā*, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra;

then, having offered one hundred and twenty-five oblations (*āhuti*) for the purpose of removing the obscuration of the *āṇava* impurity, one should resolve upon the disjunction from that impurity; and again, having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the destruction of *karman*...

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should make this request: "O Blessed One, effect the severance of these three fetters of this self, which consist of the nature of illusion, impurity, and karma; do so! Then, having cut the fetter of the *vidyā-kalā* with the mantra *hūṃ vidyākalāpāśāya haḥ hūṃ phaṭ*—uttered with its vowels while using a pair of scissors consecrated seven times with the weapon-mantra (*astra*)—one should proceed.

Having wiped it clean and rolled it into a ball, having placed it in a ladle filled with clarified butter, and having offered it as an oblation with that same mantra, one should burn it while making this petition: "O Blessed One, effect the severing of the bonds of the fetters of the *vidyā-kalā* for this self; do so! Then, once again—

Having offered five oblations with the Astra-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ* for the cessation of the sprouts of the noose (*pāśāṅkura*), and having offered eight oblations with the Astra-mantra for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should contemplate the oneness of consciousness (*caitanya*). Then, having invoked Rudra, worshipped him, and offered three oblations, one should offer three more oblations with the mantra: *Hāṃ, O you who possess the form of Rudra, accept the scent and the two *śuṣkalas*, svāhā*.
Having offered the *śuṣkala* for the purification of the *kalā*s and so forth, one should address [Rudra]:
"O Rudra, may you not obstruct the path of this traveler toward the state free from affliction."
"A restraint must be imposed"—this is the command of the Supreme Goddess.
Having thus dismissed Rudra and visualized oneself as liberated from the web of *vidyā* and *kalā*, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of extraction (*uddhāra*). Then,
having made a formal request, one should extract oneself from the fire of Rudra by means of the self-mantra (*ātma-mantra*), like an arrow released from the mouth of Rāhu.

Having spoken of oneself as resembling the lunar disc obscured by clouds, one should join [the self] with the body of the disciple-sūtra, worship it, and offer a drop of *arghya* water on the head with the root mantra for the sake of nourishment.
Then, having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of stabilization, one should fully worship the two parents, strike [the disciple], and wipe [him].

One should offer the *pūrṇāhuti*; this is the purification of the *vidyā* and *kalā* levels. At this juncture, for the purpose of examining the deceased, for the absolute severance of the subtle body (*sūkṣmadeha*), and for the complete cessation of *karman*, one should offer a hundred oblations each with the root mantra and then perform the great oblations (*mahāhuti*).
(The purification of the śāntikalā): Then follows the unification of the kalās: *hrūṃ hyaiṃ* to the two, Vidyā and Śāntikalā. (3rd line)
Having worshipped with "Namaḥ," and having offered three oblations ending with "Svāhā," one should contemplate the pure [element] dissolved into the impure; then,
having placed the Ādhāraśakti in the fire, worshipped it, and offered three oblations, [one should place it] in the location of the Sūtra-deha-Śāntikalā.

One should gaze upon that which has been attained. Thereafter: HĀṂ HYAIṂ HĀṂ, obeisance to the noose of the Śāntikalā. HĀṂ HYAIṂ HĀṂ, obeisance to the Śuddhavidyeśvara and the principles of Sadāśiva. HĀṂ HYAIṂ HĀṂ, obeisance to the eighteen worlds presided over by the powers beginning with Vāmā and ending with Icchā. HĀṂ HYAIṂ HĀṂ GA KHA KA.

Salutation to the *varṇas*. Hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ, salutation to the twelve words beginning with "dhyānāhārādi" and ending with "vyomavyāpinaḥ. Hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ haiṃ heṃ, salutation to the two mantras of the *kavaca* and the *tatpuruṣa*. Hāṃ hyaiṃ hāṃ ya...

Salutation to the Seed-syllable (*bīja*). Hāṃ Hyaiṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Yaśā and the Alambuṣā channel. Hāṃ Hyaiṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Kṛkara and Kūrma, the two vital airs (*vāyu*). Hāṃ Hyaiṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the sense-organ of touch and the feet. Hāṃ Hyaiṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the object of touch. Hāṃ Hrūṃ (Hyaiṃ).

Hāṃ, obeisance to the two qualities of touch and sound. Hāṃ hyaiṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the black wind-maṇḍala, which possesses six points, has six corners, and measures one hundred thousand crores of *yojanas*.
Hāṃ hyaiṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the cause that is Īśvara. Having thus worshipped the dark [deity], and having taken up [the breath] through the *pūraka* and *saṃhāriṇī* [processes]... (2nd line)
Having joined the thread from the mouth to the heart, having worshipped it, restrained it, and veiled it, and having also worshipped it in the fire,

one should offer five oblations for the sake of its presence. Thereafter, [one should contemplate] the two bonds consisting of the impurity of limited agency (*āṇavamala*) and *māyā*, which have been purified.

Having contemplated [the principle] as the generator of the enjoyer, the body of enjoyment, and so forth, one should worship with the mantra *hāṃ īśvarakāraṇeśvarāya namaḥ*, offer three oblations, and having made the formal request, one should conceive of the various bodies, such as those of the bindu-nature, within that *kalā* according to the ripening of impurity (*mala*) for birth in various wombs.
Having worshipped Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśa, who pervade that [mantra], and having caused them to be present and made a formal request, he should sprinkle the disciple with the Astra-mantra,
seize him according to the previous sequence of striking and so forth, expel him, and contemplate the union of the two parents.

Having performed the simultaneous union of oneself with all wombs (*yoni*) in the form of manifold manifestations by means of the *utbhavamudrā* of the left hand and one’s own mantra, and having worshipped [them], one should offer three oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*). Having made a formal request for the completion of all embryos, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and contemplate their dissolution (*laya*). Then, for the sake of birth, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra.

Having requested [the deities] for the sake of their authorization (*adhikāra*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra; having requested them for the sake of enjoyment (*bhoga*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra; having requested them and contemplated their dissolution (*laya*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra; having requested them for the purification of the streams (*srotas*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra; and having requested them for the purification of the reality of peace (*śāntitatva-śuddhi*), one should offer three oblations into the heart with the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*).
Having offered one hundred oblations with the *kavaca* and the *pūrva-prāsāda* mantras for the sake of expiation,

and having contemplated the separation of the self from the fetter of impure *māyā*, O Blessed One, he should offer three oblations with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) while meditating upon his [new] authority; then, for the purpose of concealing that [old authority], he should offer ten oblations with the root mantra, thereby effecting the separation from it.

Having honored [the deity] with the root mantra, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*). One should then make this request: "O Blessed One, effect the separation of the impurity of office (*adhikāra-mala*) belonging to this self, which is pure illusion (*śuddha-māyeya*); *kuru kuru* (do, do)! Then, with a pair of scissors consecrated seven times with the weapon mantra (*astra*), [one recites]: *hyaiṃ śāntikalāpāśāya haḥ*.
Uttering "Hūṃ Phaṭ" with its proper resonance, one should cut the noose of the Śāntikalā with both hands, release it while reciting the mantra, form it into a circle,
place it in a *sruva* ladle filled with clarified butter, and having offered it with that same mantra, one should burn it. O Blessed One, for this self...

One should request, "Perform the severing of the noose of the *śāntikalā*! Perform! Then, for the sake of removing the noose and the goad, one should offer five oblations with the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*, and eight oblations with the expiatory mantra; [this is done] for the destruction of the entire body.

Having contemplated the oneness of consciousness, having invoked and worshipped the Lord, and having offered oblations for His presence, one should offer three oblations for the purpose of purifying the elemental body, saying: "Hāṃ! O Lord, intellect and ego, accept [this], svāhā!
(5th line)
He should inform [the Lord]:
"O Lord, you must not place any obstacle in the path of this traveler;
such is the command of the Supreme Goddess."
Having thus released this [impurity] and contemplated the pure self, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of extraction. Then,

having requested, "O Blessed One, perform the extraction of this self from the bond of the *śāntikalā*," one should extract [the self] from the fire of Raudrī by means of the *saṃhāriṇī* [mantra] and the inhalation (*pūraka*).
Having brought the Self, which resembles the stainless autumn moon, into the heart of one's own self,

and having joined it to the body of the disciple’s thread by means of the *recaka* breath and the *udbhava-mudrā*, and having worshipped it, one should cast a drop of *arghya* water upon the head of the disciple with the root mantra for the sake of nourishment and for the purpose of stabilization.

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra, having fully worshipped the parents, having gratified them, and having honored them with arghya, one should dismiss them and offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti). Thus ends the purification of the Śāntikalā.
(The purification of the kalā beyond peace. Then follows the unification of the kalās.

Having worshipped with "Hyaiṃ Hauṃ, obeisance to the two kalās, Śānti and Śāntyatīta," and having offered three oblations while contemplating that the pure [kalā] has dissolved into the impure, one should invoke Śāntyatītā. Then, having placed the Ādhāraśakti in the fire and worshipped her, and having offered three oblations, [one should place her] in the Sūtra-body at the station of Śāntyatītā.

One should observe its pervasion. Thereafter: HĀM HAUM HĀM, obeisance to the bond of the Śāntyatīta-kalā; HĀM HAUM HĀM, obeisance to the Śiva-tattva and Śakti-tattva; HĀM HAUM HĀM, obeisance to the fifteen worlds presided over by the powers beginning with Nivṛtti and ending with Anāśrita. (Third line)

Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ! Salutation to the sixteen phonemes beginning with *aḥ* and ending with *a*. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ! Salutation to the state of the *Oṃkāra*, which is beyond all, transcending the fourth (*turyātīta*). Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ! Haḥ! Salutation to the mantras of Astrarudra, Śiva, and Īśāna.

Salutation! Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the seed-syllable Hakāra. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Śaṅkhinī and the Kuhū-nāḍī. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the winds Dhanañjaya and Devadatta. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ...

Salutation to the organ of speech and the sense of hearing. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the object of sound. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the quality of resonance. Hāṃ Hauṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the sphere of space (*vyomamaṇḍala*), which has the appearance of crystal and whose essence is the element of vacuity. Salutation to the power of *bindu* and *nāda*, which is self-spherical and measures eighty million *koṭis* of *yojanas*.

HĀṂ HAUṂ HĀṂ, obeisance to Sadāśiva, the Cause. Having worshipped [the mantra] whose nature consists of the *pratikha*, the *svarūpa*, the white crescent moon, the *bindu*, the *nāda*, and the *kuṭila*, and having grasped it with the *pūraka-saṃhāriṇī* [mudrā],

one should join it to the thread extending from the crest (*cūḍā*) to the forehead (*lalāṭa*), worship it there, restrain it, veil it, and worship it again in the fire for the sake of its presence (*sannidhāna*).

(127b, 1st line) One should offer five oblations. Thereafter, having meditated upon the pure form of Māyā as the substrate of authority, one should invoke Sadāśiva, the Lord of Causes; having worshipped him and caused him to become present, and having made the request, [one should [extract him] from his manifold bodies into that *kalā*.

Having performed the visualization, having worshipped Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara who pervade that [deity], having offered oblations for their presence and invoked their proximity, and having prayed [to them] and sprinkled the disciple with the Astra-mantra;

With that flower ending in *huṃ phaṭ*, having entered his body at the heart by means of the syllable *huṃ*, and having separated [the soul], one should draw it out with the mantra of oneself ending in *svāhā* and lead it to the *dvādaśānta*. Having visualized the life-force (*jīva*) as resembling the autumn moon, one should grasp it with the mantra of oneself, place it within the heart, and form a vessel (*kumbha*) with the mantra of oneself.

Having led [the seed-syllable] to the *dvādaśānta* by means of the sequence of abandoning the causal deities beginning with Brahmā, having gathered it and expelled it, and having visualized the union of the parents,
one should simultaneously effect the union of the self with its own mantra in the form of manifold manifestations through the *udbhavamudrā* of the left [nostril].

Having performed [the rite] with the root mantra, having worshipped, and having offered three oblations, one should inform [the deity] for the sake of the complete formation of the entire body; having offered three oblations with the root mantra and made a request, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of birth; having informed [the deity] and offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of authority, one should inform [the deity]; having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of enjoyment and made a request, one should contemplate dissolution.

Having offered three oblations with the *mūla-mantra* and made a request for the purification of the channels (*srotas*), and having performed three oblations with the *mūla-mantra* and made a request for the purification of the principles (*tattva*) beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*), one should offer three oblations with the *hṛdaya-mantra*. Having offered one hundred oblations with the *mūla-mantra* for the sake of expiation (*niṣkṛti*), [one should offer] three oblations with the *mūla-mantra* for the purpose of severing the bonds of Mahāmāyā.

Having offered ten oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of removing the impurity of the authority (*adhikāra-mala*), and having given three oblations with the root mantra for its separation, one should make this request: "O Blessed One, effect the separation of this self, which consists of the impurity of the authority of Great Māyā (*mahāmāyādhikāra-mala*); do so, do so! Then, [one should act] with [the water] over which the weapon-mantra (*astra*) has been recited seven times.
With the *kartarī* [knife], one should chant "Hauṃ" (second line),
then "Haḥ Huṃ Phaṭ" with the vowels for the purpose of severing the bonds (*pāśa*) of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*. Having severed the bonds of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*,
one should wipe it with the *astra-mantra*, roll it into a circle, place it in a *sruc* ladle filled with clarified butter, and having offered it with that same mantra, one should burn it.

(Third line) Having petitioned, "O Blessed One, perform, perform the cutting of the bonds of this self that have transcended the stage of peace," one should offer five oblations with the *astra-mantra* ending in *huṃ phaṭ* for the cessation of the sprouts of the bonds, and eight oblations with the *astra-mantra* for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), [and then] for the destruction of the entire body...
Having contemplated the unity of consciousness, one should invoke Sadāśiva, the Lord of Causes, with the root mantra, worship him, and establish his presence; [then,
for the purification of the body consisting of the Bindu, one should utter] *Hauṃ*.
"O Blessed One, accept the mind-drop as the bride-price, svāhā! Having offered the bride-price with these three oblations,
one should make this request.

"This one, who brings about auspiciousness and has transcended the most excellent [state], has now accomplished his purpose; having brought about the cessation of even the slightest rebirth, I shall show him compassion.
Having thus dismissed him, [he places him] at the summit of the pure principles.
Having visualized [the self] as being like a pure crystal gem, utterly stainless, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra to effect its extraction.

Having made this request, one should extract the self from the fire of Raudrī by means of the ātma-mantra through inhalation (*pūraka*), and [perceive] the self, which is the manifestation of the nature of existence and consciousness, residing in the heart of one's own self.

Having visualized [the deities] through exhalation (*recaka*), having joined them to the body of the disciple's thread, and having worshipped them, one should cast a drop of *arghya* water upon the head;
then, for the sake of stabilization, having offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should worship and satiate the two *pitaras*.
Thus urged regarding the initiation of the disciple: "O you two *pitaras*, that which has been performed by me..."

"Out of compassion, forgive that which was done by me as I depart for my own abode. Having made this request and dismissed [the deity], one should offer the *pūrṇāhuti*. Thus concludes the purification of the bond of the *kalā* beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*).
(The Ritual for Cutting the Topknot):

Afterwards, having joined [the disciple] with the Tirodhāyikā Śakti while reciting "Obeisance to Śānti and Atīta Śakti," one should [perform] the three principles (*tattva*) for the sake of expiation.

Having established [the fire] as pervading up to the principles of Māyā, Vidyā, and Śiva, one should offer a hundred oblations each by means of the family of utterances— spoken, whispered, and mental— to purify any deficiency in the ritual procedure, deficiency in the worship of the mantra, and deficiency in the mental state, and also to purify the power of concealment (*tirodhāna-śakti*).

Having performed one hundred oblations with the root mantra and having visualized the consciousness residing at the tip [of the blade] up to the level of Śiva, one should sever the topknot with a sickle consecrated seven times by Śiva, reciting: *hrūṃ śikhāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.
Having placed [the vessel] wrapped in cow dung at the tip of the blade of grass and having offered oblations and satisfied [the deity] with that same mantra, [the method of self-union is as follows:
"O Great Goddess, by Your will, a transgression has been committed through another womb."
Let him be released by your will; O Lord of the World, do not obstruct him.
"By your will, this purified one shall attain the state of Śiva through the transposition [of the elements].
Having thus informed Śiva, he should take hold of the disciple's self as before and bring it into his own heart.

Having brought about a state of equanimity (*samarasībhāva*) by means of the conch-like mudrā (*śaṅkhasannibhamudrā*), and having taken up the clarified butter with the sacrificial ladle (*sruc*) and spoon (*sruva*),

one should rise while recollecting Śiva, who pervades all paths; then, through the unity of the disciple’s self, vital breath, and mind, one should recollect the flow of the *nāda* within the *suṣumnā*.
Having contemplated the consciousness of the disciple as resembling a perfected crystal gem, while reciting the mantra according to the path taught by the Guru,
the Lord of Causes gradually abandons [the levels], his powers and parts becoming tranquil and dissolved.

Recalling the stream of clarified butter (*sarpiṣo dhārām*), one releases it into Śiva— who is beyond the seven [levels], beyond the power (*śakti*), at the end of the twelve (*dvādaśānta*), and beyond the mind (*manotīta*)— who is indivisible in form, existence, consciousness, and bliss, non-dual and perfectly full; just as water poured into water, milk into milk, or ghee into ghee.
Otherwise, there would be no distinction; for the self would then be identical with the supreme Self.

One should unite [the soul]. Now, if [the soul] is of slow maturation, one should—according to the degree of ripening of its impurities—unite the self with the three principles beginning with Śuddhavidyā, or with the principles and worlds of Bindu and Nāda, so that it remains until the dissolution of the universe, endowed with the six qualities, free from even a trace of suffering, and rejoicing like Śiva; and then, by means of oblations of clarified butter poured into the fire...

*Tisṛbhuḥ* (... *bhiḥ hauṃ*, O Self, become omniscient, svāhā! Thus, become completely satisfied; become awakened from beginningless time; become independent in being; become possessed of unimpaired power;
become possessed of infinite power.

Thus, having brought forth the qualities and having united the corpse situated on the sacrificial ground with that which resides in the fire, one should release the corpse. (The procedure for cremation and so forth. The corpse... (line 9)

Having placed the head toward the south upon the mind-line, covered it with a new cloth, sealed it with good fuel, and having kindled it with fire not yet abandoned from the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should lift up a ladle (*sruva*) filled with ghee, honey, and milk at the location of the head.
"O Agni, you are the southern quarter;
accept this Śamī wood, consecrated by mantras and brought here at the proper time, for the sake of the great rite."
Having offered the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), if he is the preceptor (*ācārya*), he should cast the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles face-down on his left and right sides;

if they are the practitioner (*sādhaka*) or the grandson (*pautra*), they should cast them into the funeral pyre itself. Then, the son [should offer] four auspicious [oblations] into the consecrated fire.

Having employed the vardhanī vessel and placed it upon his left shoulder, releasing an unbroken stream directed away from him while moving against the wind, he should circumambulate [the site] counter-clockwise, deposit it in its proper place with the opening facing downwards, and then not look back. He should then proceed to the reservoir.

This is the procedure for one who has received the initiation of liberation (*nirvāṇadīkṣā*) and desires it, as well as for one who serves the Guru and for the initiation of the deceased (*mṛtadīkṣā*). Then, having bathed and spread *kuśa* grass on the bank, [he offers] three handfuls of water-libations (*nivāpa-añjali*): "Hāṃ! O Pure Self, become a portion; *svadhā*. Hāṃ! O Pure Self, become Sadāśiva; *svadhā*."

Having offered [the oblation] with "Hāṃ! O pure Self, be peaceful; Svadhā!", and having bathed again, the followers, the reciters of the Saṃhitā, the Aghora-mantra, and the hundred [recitations], as well as the donors and the cremators, should each recite twice as much.
Having cremated the corpse of one who is not a relative, or having offered a funeral cake (skandha) for one who is pure,
one should bathe, mutter the Rūpī-mantra two hundred times, and after plunging [into water], worship the Lord.
One should not follow a person of low caste even if he is observant of vows;
having followed him, one should bathe at the edge of the water and recite the *Śata* [the hundred-syllable mantra] belonging to one's own caste.
One who is established in a vow [should not follow] another who is established in a vow, or a Brahmin initiated into the Śiva-vow.
Whoever carries one who has perished shall not suffer an untimely death.
He who takes a deceased Śiva-yogin— who is without companion and without protector—
and bathes him, is liberated from all calamities.
(The sequence beginning with the entry into one's own abode.)

Thereafter, having cast off his sorrow, he went to the door of the house, ate neem leaves, performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), touched fire, water, cow dung, and white mustard seeds, and having placed [the items] down, he entered the temple and [touched] a stone.

In honor of the deceased, they should perform worship and, excluding savory foods, take as their sustenance for life what has been offered by one another during the afternoon. (Regarding the expiation for when the funeral rites have not been performed:
Now, if for some reason the funeral rites have not been performed, one should perform a substitute rite. For example, with *darbha* grass... (line 8).

Having fashioned an image either from flour mixed with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) or from pure cow dung, and having performed the sacrifice as before— preceded by the invocation of the deity and the preparation of the site— one should bathe the effigy with the five products of the cow and auspicious water, and place it to the south of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having established [the deity] with *karavīra* buds at the location of the subtle body (*sūkṣmadeha*), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the principles (*tattvas*), their presiding deities, and their lords, preceded by the utterance of the heart-seed syllable (*hṛdbīja*). Above the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), [one should place]: "Hauṃ, obeisance to Rodhaśakti. At the aperture of Brahmā: "Hāṃ... (line 10).
Salutation to the Śiva-tattva, whose form is the Bindu. HAUṂ, salutation to Śiva, the lord of the Śiva-tattva. That which is the Brahma-randhra at the crown of the head.
HĀṂ, salutation to the Śakti-tattva. HĀṂ, salutation to Śaktimān, the lord of the Śakti-tattva. That which is above the Khaṇḍikā of the head.

Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Sadāśiva. Hāṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the lord of the principle of Sadāśiva, from the uvula to the shoulders. Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Īśvara. Hāṃ, salutation to Ananta, the lord of the principle of Īśvara. Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Vidyā. (Second line)
Salutation! Hāṃ, salutation to Śambara, the lord of the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva). On the left side: Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of illusion (māyā-tattva);

Hāṃ, salutation to Gahaneśa, the lord of the principle of illusion. On the right side: Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of time (kāla-tattva); Hāṃ, salutation to the lord of the principle of time. (Third line)
Salutation to Kāla by name. On the chest: Hāṃ, salutation to Kalātattva; Hāṃ, salutation to Jñānabindu, the lord of Kalātattva.
In the heart: Hāṃ, salutation to Niyatitattva; Hāṃ, salutation to Niyāmaka, the lord of Niyatitattva. Hāṃ, salutation to Vidyātattva. Hāṃ... (fourth line).

Salutation to the Lord of the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*), the knower of the Vedas. Hāṃ! Salutation to the principle of the person (*puruṣa-tattva*). Hāṃ! Salutation to the Lord of the principle of the person, the subtle body (*sūkṣma-deha*). Hāṃ! Salutation to the principle of passion (*rāga-tattva*). Hāṃ! Salutation to the Lord of the principle of passion, the bestower of desires (*kāma-da*). (Fifth line)

In the abdomen: [OṂ] *namaḥ* to the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti-tattva*). *Hāṃ*, *namaḥ* to the Lord of the principle of primordial nature, the body of Pradhāna. In the spinal column: [OṂ] *namaḥ* to the principle of the qualities (*guṇa-tattva*). *Hāṃ*, *namaḥ* to the Lord of the principle of the qualities, the three-bodied one (*tri-deha*).
Between the navel and the genitals: *Hāṃ*. (Sixth line)

Salutation to the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*). Hāṃ, salutation to the Buddha, the lord of the principle of intellect. At the three joints (–): Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of ego (*ahaṅkāratattva*). Hāṃ, salutation to Ahaṅkṛti, the lord of the principle of ego. Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of mind (*manastattva*). Hāṃ (7th line), salutation to Saṃkalpa, the lord of the principle of mind. In the ear (–): Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of hearing (*śrotratattva*).

Hāṃ, homage to the Lord of the principle of hearing, the sky-farer. In the skin: Hāṃ, homage to the principle of the skin. Hāṃ, homage to the Lord of the principle of the skin, the one who pervades all limbs. (8th line)

In the two eyes: *hāṃ*, homage to the reality of the eye (*cakṣustattva*); *hāṃ*, homage to Prakāśa, the lord of the reality of the eye (*cakṣustattvādhipa*).
